title.zh: 卷六十四 列傳第二十四 鄭鮮之 裴松之 何承天
title.en: Volume 64 Biographies 24: Zheng Xianzhi, Pei Songzhi, He Chengtian
title.raw: 卷六十四 列傳第二十四 鄭鮮之 裴松之 何承天 Volume 64 Biographies 24: Zheng Xianzhi, Pei Songzhi, He Chengtian

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十四 鄭鮮之裴松之何承天

translations.literal: Biographies 24: Zheng Xianzhi, Pei Songzhi, and He Chengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Biography 24: Zheng Xianzhi, Pei Songzhi, and He Chengtian.

sentences.zh: 鄭鮮之，字道子，滎陽開封人也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xianzhi, courtesy name Daozi, was a native of Kaifeng in Yingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xianzhi, whose courtesy name was Daozi, came from Kaifeng in Yingyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖渾，魏將作大匠。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Hun was Director of Palace Construction in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Hun had served the Wei court as Director of Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: 曾祖襲，大司農。

translations.literal: His great-great-grandfather Xi was Grand Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: His great-great-grandfather Xi had held the post of Grand Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 父遵，尚書郎。

translations.literal: His father Zun was a Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zun had been a Gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 襲初為江乘令，因居縣境。

translations.literal: Xi had first been magistrate of Jiangcheng, and the family therefore settled within that county.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi first served as magistrate of Jiangcheng, the family settled in that county and remained there.

sentences.zh: 鮮之下帷讀書，絕交遊之務。

translations.literal: Xianzhi drew his curtains and studied, cutting off all social engagements.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi shut himself in to read and refused every distraction of society and friendship.

sentences.zh: 初為桓偉輔國主簿。

translations.literal: He first served as Registrar of the State-supporting Army under Huan Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His first appointment was as chief clerk to Huan Wei, general who supported the state.

sentences.zh: 先是，兗州刺史滕恬為丁零、翟遼所沒，尸喪不反，恬子羨仕宦不廢，議者嫌之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Teng Tian, Inspector of Yan province, had been killed by the Dingling and Zhai Liao, and his corpse had not been recovered; yet Tian's son Xian did not cease his official career, and critics found this objectionable.
translations.idiomatic: Some time before, Teng Tian, regional inspector of Yan, had fallen to the Dingling and Zhai Liao, and his body was never brought home. His son Xian nevertheless continued in office without interruption, which many found hard to accept.

sentences.zh: 桓玄在荊州，使群僚博議，鮮之議曰：

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan was in Jing province, he had his staff debate the matter broadly; Xianzhi offered this opinion:
translations.idiomatic: While Huan Xuan held Jing province, he ordered a wide deliberation among his officials. Xianzhi argued as follows:

sentences.zh: 名教大極，忠孝而已，至乎變通抑引，每事輒殊，本而尋之，皆是求心而遺跡。

translations.literal: The supreme pole of moral teaching is nothing but loyalty and filial piety; as for adaptation, restraint, and promotion, each affair differs, yet traced to the root they all seek the heart while leaving the traces behind.
translations.idiomatic: The highest aim of ritual and moral teaching is loyalty and filial piety alone. When one must bend, restrain, or exalt conduct, each case differs; yet at bottom the sages always looked to the inward motive and set the outward act aside.

sentences.zh: 跡之所乘，遭遇或異。

translations.literal: What the traces ride upon may meet with different circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: The deeds that follow depend on circumstances, and those circumstances may differ widely.

sentences.zh: 故聖人或就跡以助教，或因跡以成罪，屈申與奪，難可等齊，舉其阡陌，皆可略言矣。

translations.literal: Therefore the sages sometimes took the traces to reinforce teaching, and sometimes used the traces to establish guilt; bending, extending, granting, and withholding cannot be made equal—yet surveying their paths, all may be spoken of in brief.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the sages sometimes upheld the outward act to reinforce a lesson and sometimes condemned it to establish guilt. To bend, extend, reward, or punish cannot be reduced to one rule; still, if we survey their various paths, each can be outlined in brief.

sentences.zh: 天可逃乎？

translations.literal: Can Heaven be fled?
translations.idiomatic: Can anyone flee from Heaven's mandate?

sentences.zh: 而伊尹廢君；

translations.literal: Yet Yi Yin deposed his ruler;
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yi Yin deposed his lord;

sentences.zh: 君可脅乎？

translations.literal: Can a ruler be coerced?
translations.idiomatic: Can a ruler be compelled by force?

sentences.zh: 而鬻權見善；

translations.literal: Yet Yu Quan showed goodness;
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yu Quan was praised for his goodness;

sentences.zh: 忠可愚乎？

translations.literal: Can loyalty be foolish?
translations.idiomatic: Can loyalty be called folly?

sentences.zh: 而箕子同仁。

translations.literal: Yet Jizi shared the same hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jizi endured the same fate as a fellow sufferer.

sentences.zh: 自此以還，殊實而齊聲，異譽而等美者，不可勝言。

translations.literal: From this onward, cases of different substance given equal praise, or different reputations held equally fine, cannot be told in full.
translations.idiomatic: From that point on, examples of unlike deeds praised alike, or unlike reputations judged equally noble, are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 而欲令百代之下，聖典所闕，正斯事於一朝，豈可易哉！

translations.literal: Yet to wish that a hundred generations hence, where the sacred canon is silent, this matter be settled in a single morning—how could that be easy!
translations.idiomatic: To expect that what the sages left undecided should be settled once and for all in our own day, a hundred generations later—surely that cannot be done lightly!

sentences.zh: 然立言明理，以古證今，當使理厭人情。

translations.literal: Yet in setting forth words and clarifying principle, using antiquity to test the present, principle should satisfy human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Still, when one states a doctrine and clarifies principle, using the past to judge the present, reason must fully satisfy what human feeling demands.

sentences.zh: 如滕羨情事者，或終身隱處，不關人事；

translations.literal: In a case like Teng Xian's, one might spend life in seclusion and have nothing to do with public affairs;
translations.idiomatic: In a case like Teng Xian's, a man might withdraw for life and have no part in public affairs;

sentences.zh: 或升朝理務，無譏前哲。

translations.literal: or enter court and manage affairs without censure from the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: or he might enter court and take up office without drawing censure from the sages of old.

sentences.zh: 通滕者則以無譏為證，塞滕者則以隱處為美。

translations.literal: Those who would clear Teng cite the lack of censure as proof; those who would block him cite seclusion as the ideal.
translations.idiomatic: Those who would excuse Teng point to the absence of ancient censure; those who would condemn him hold up lifelong withdrawal as the proper model.

sentences.zh: 折其兩中，則異同之情可見矣。

translations.literal: Split the difference between the two, and the grounds of agreement and disagreement become visible.
translations.idiomatic: Split the difference between the two sides, and the true points of agreement and dispute will stand clear.

sentences.zh: 然無譏前哲者，厭情之謂也。

translations.literal: Yet 'no censure from the ancients' means that feeling is satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when one says the ancients did not censure such conduct, one means only that human feeling is satisfied—not that the act is beyond question.

sentences.zh: 若王陵之母，見烹于楚，陵不退身窮居，終為社稷之臣，非為榮也。

translations.literal: Consider Wang Ling's mother, who was boiled alive by Chu: Ling did not withdraw to live in poverty, but in the end became a minister of the altars of soil and grain—not for glory.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ling's mother was boiled alive by Chu, yet Ling did not retire into seclusion; in the end he served the state—not for honor or gain, but from duty.

sentences.zh: 鮑勳蹇諤魏朝，亡身為效，觀其志非貪爵也。

translations.literal: Bao Xun spoke bluntly in the Wei court and lost his life in service; viewed by his intent, he did not covet rank.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xun spoke bluntly at the Wei court and gave his life in loyal service; his aim was plainly not to win rank or reward.

sentences.zh: 凡此二賢，非滕之諭。

translations.literal: Both these worthy men are no parallel for Teng.
translations.idiomatic: These two worthies offer no real parallel to Teng Xian's case.

sentences.zh: 夫聖人立教，猶雲「有禮無時，君子不行」。

translations.literal: When the sages established teaching, they even said, 'Where there is ritual but not the right time, the gentleman does not act.'
translations.idiomatic: In establishing moral teaching, the sages even said that where ritual exists but the time is wrong, a gentleman should not act.

sentences.zh: 有禮無時，政以事有變通，不可守一故耳。

translations.literal: 'Ritual without the right time' means precisely that affairs admit adaptation and one cannot cling to a single rule.
translations.idiomatic: 'Ritual without the right time' means that affairs must be adapted and one cannot cling to a single fixed rule.

sentences.zh: 若滕以此二賢為證，則恐人人自賢矣；

translations.literal: If Teng cites these two worthies as proof, I fear every man will deem himself worthy;
translations.idiomatic: If Teng may cite these two worthies in his defense, then every man will think himself a sage;

sentences.zh: 若不可人人自賢，何可獨許其證。

translations.literal: if not every man may deem himself worthy, how can his proof alone be allowed?
translations.idiomatic: and if not every man may call himself worthy, how can Teng alone be allowed this argument?

sentences.zh: 譏者兼在於人，不但獨證其事。

translations.literal: Censure rests on the person as well, not on proving the affair alone.
translations.idiomatic: Censure bears on the person himself, not on a single precedent drawn from the act alone.

sentences.zh: 漢、魏以來，記闕其典，尋而得者……無幾人。

translations.literal: From Han and Wei onward, records omit the standard; of those later found … very few.
translations.idiomatic: From Han and Wei onward the records omit clear precedent, and of those later recovered … there are very few indeed.

sentences.zh: 至乎大晉中朝及中興之後，楊臻則七年不除喪，三十餘年不關人事，溫公則見逼於王命，庾左丞則終身不著袷，高世遠則為王右軍、何驃騎所勸割，無有如滕之易者也。

translations.literal: As for the central court of Great Jin and after the Restoration: Yang Zhen observed mourning for seven years without leaving it and for more than thirty years had nothing to do with public affairs; Wen Gong was pressed by the king's command; the Left Assistant Minister Yu never wore lined garments in his life; Gao Shiyuan was urged by Wang the General of the Right Army and He the Cavalry General to shorten mourning—none was as easy as Teng.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jin central court and after the Restoration, Yang Zhen kept mourning for seven years and for more than thirty years stayed out of public life; Wen Gong was compelled by royal command; Assistant Minister Yu never wore lined garments to the end of his days; Gao Shiyuan was urged by Wang Xizhi and He the Cavalry General to shorten his mourning—yet none took office as lightly as Teng Xian did.

sentences.zh: 若以縗麻非為哀之主，無所復言矣。

translations.literal: If coarse hemp is not held to be the chief expression of grief, nothing more need be said.
translations.idiomatic: If one holds that coarse hemp garments are not the chief sign of grief, then there is nothing more to argue.

sentences.zh: 文皇帝以東關之役，屍骸不反者，制其子弟，不廢婚宦。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen, because of the Battle of Dongguan where corpses were not recovered, regulated the sons and younger brothers so that marriage and office were not abolished.
translations.idiomatic: After the Battle of Dongguan, when many bodies were never recovered, Emperor Wen decreed that the sons and younger brothers of the fallen need not give up marriage or office.

sentences.zh: 明此，孝子已不自同於人倫，有識已審其可否矣。

translations.literal: Once this is clear, a filial son already does not set himself apart from human relations, and the discerning have already judged what is permissible.
translations.idiomatic: Once this is understood, a filial son no longer sets himself outside ordinary human ties, and the discerning have already judged what may or may not be done.

sentences.zh: 若其不爾，居宗輔物者，但當即聖人之教，何所復明制於其間哉！

translations.literal: If it were not so, those who dwell in the lineage and assist in affairs need only follow the sages' teaching—what further need to clarify regulations among them!
translations.idiomatic: If it were otherwise, men of lineage who serve the state need only follow the sages' teaching—why should new regulations be spelled out for them at all?

sentences.zh: 及至永嘉大亂之後，王敦復申東關之制於中興，原此是為國之大計，非謂訓範人倫，盡於此也。

translations.literal: When after the great disorder of Yongjia, Wang Dun again proclaimed the Dongguan regulation at the Restoration, the origin of this was a great plan for the state, not that moral instruction for mankind was exhausted in it.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongjia upheaval, Wang Dun revived the Dongguan rule during the Restoration—but that was a measure for the survival of the state, not a claim that all moral teaching for mankind was summed up in it.

sentences.zh: 何以言之？

translations.literal: How may this be said?
translations.idiomatic: How can one say this?

sentences.zh: 父仇明不同戴天日，而為國不可許復仇，此自以法奪情，即是東關、永嘉之喻也。

translations.literal: A father's enemy plainly cannot share heaven and earth with one, yet for the state revenge cannot be permitted—this itself uses law to override feeling, and is precisely the lesson of Dongguan and Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: A father's murderer cannot live under the same sky with his son, yet the state may not permit private revenge—law must override private feeling. That is exactly the lesson of Dongguan and Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 何妨綜理王務者，布衣以處之。

translations.literal: What harm if one who oversees royal affairs is treated as a commoner in dress?
translations.idiomatic: What harm if a man who still manages state affairs is treated, in outward status, like a commoner?

sentences.zh: 明教者自謂世非橫流，凡士君子之徒，無不可仕之理，而雜以情譏，謂宜在貶裁爾。

translations.literal: Those who clarify teaching suppose the age is not a torrent in flood; all gentlemen have no reason they may not serve, yet mixed with emotional censure, they say one ought to be demoted and judged.
translations.idiomatic: Those who uphold moral teaching assume the age is not utterly chaotic and that no gentleman is barred in principle from office—yet they mix in personal censure and say he ought to be demoted and judged.

sentences.zh: 若多引前事以為通證，則孝子可顧法而不復仇矣。

translations.literal: If many past cases are cited as general proof, then a filial son may look to law and not avenge.
translations.idiomatic: If one may cite many past cases as general precedent, then every filial son could appeal to law and forgo revenge.

sentences.zh: 文皇帝無所立制於東關，王敦無所明之於中興。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen established no regulation at Dongguan, and Wang Dun clarified nothing at the Restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen laid down no lasting rule at Dongguan, and Wang Dun proclaimed no clear doctrine at the Restoration.

sentences.zh: 每至斯會，輒發之於宰物，是心可不喻乎！

translations.literal: Whenever such a juncture arose, they would entrust it to those who govern affairs—is that intent not plain!
translations.idiomatic: Whenever such a crisis arose, they left the matter to those who governed the realm—their intent should be plain enough!

sentences.zh: 且夫求理當先以遠大，若滄海橫流，家國同其淪溺，若不仕也，則人有餘力；

translations.literal: Moreover, in seeking principle one should begin with what is far-reaching and great: if the blue sea flows across the land and family and state sink together, if men do not serve, then people have surplus strength;
translations.idiomatic: In seeking principle one must begin with the larger view. When the realm is flooded like the sea and family and state sink together, if men refuse office, each keeps his strength to himself;

sentences.zh: 人有餘力，則國可至乎亡，家可至乎滅。

translations.literal: if people have surplus strength, then the state may come to ruin and the family to extinction.
translations.idiomatic: and when each keeps his strength, the state may perish and the clan be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 當斯時也，匹婦猶亡其身，況大丈夫哉！

translations.literal: At such a time, even a common woman will lose her life—how much more a great man!
translations.idiomatic: In such a time even an ordinary woman will give her life—how much more should a man of stature!

sentences.zh: 既其不然，天下之才，將無所理。

translations.literal: Since it is not so, the talents of the realm will have nowhere to be ordered.
translations.idiomatic: If that were not so, the talents of the realm would have nowhere to be put to use.

sentences.zh: 滕但當盡《陟岵》之哀，擬不仕者之心，何為證喻前人，以自通乎？

translations.literal: Teng need only fulfill the grief of 'Ascending the Hill,' matching the heart of one who does not serve—why cite and compare forebears to clear himself?
translations.idiomatic: Teng need only fulfill the grief expressed in the 'Ascending the Hill' ode and share the mind of one who refuses office—why must he cite forebears to justify himself?

sentences.zh: 且名為大才之所假，而小才之所榮，榮與假乘常，已有慚德，無欣工進，何有情事乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, fame is what great talent borrows and small talent glorifies; glory and borrowing ride together as the norm—already there is shame in virtue, no joy in advancing through merit—what room for personal feeling?
translations.idiomatic: Office is what great talent borrows and small talent prizes as glory; when glory and pretense ride together as the norm, shame already attaches to one's conduct, and there is no joy in advancing through merit—what personal motive can there be?

sentences.zh: 若其不然，則工進無欣，何足貴於千載之上邪！

translations.literal: If it were not so, then advancing through merit without joy—how could that be prized a thousand years hence!
translations.idiomatic: If it were otherwise, then advancing through merit without joy—how could that be honored a thousand years later!

sentences.zh: 苟許小才榮其位，則滕不當顧常疑以自居乎。

translations.literal: If small talent may glorify its post, should Teng not always look back in doubt upon himself?
translations.idiomatic: If small talent may take glory in office, should Teng not live in constant self-doubt?

sentences.zh: 所謂柳下惠則可，我則不可也。

translations.literal: As the saying goes, 'Liuxia Hui could do it; I cannot.'
translations.idiomatic: As the saying goes, Liuxia Hui might do such a thing—but I could not.

sentences.zh: 且有生之所宗者聖人，聖人之為教者禮法，即心而言，則聖人之法，不可改也。

translations.literal: Moreover, what the living revere is the sage; what the sage establishes as teaching is ritual and law; speaking from the heart, the sage's law cannot be altered.
translations.idiomatic: What all living beings revere is the sage, and what the sage teaches is ritual and law. In the heart's judgment, the sage's law cannot be changed.

sentences.zh: 而秦以郡縣治天下，莫之能變；

translations.literal: Yet Qin governed the realm with commanderies and counties, and none could change it;
translations.idiomatic: Yet Qin governed the realm through commanderies and counties, and none could restore the old order;

sentences.zh: 漢文除肉刑，莫之能復。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han abolished corporal mutilation, and none could restore it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han abolished corporal mutilation, and none could bring it back.

sentences.zh: 彼聖人之為法，猶見改於後王，況滕賴前人，而當必通乎？

translations.literal: Even the sages' laws were altered by later kings—how much more must Teng, relying on forebears, be cleared without question?
translations.idiomatic: Even the sages' laws were changed by later kings—how then can Teng, leaning on past examples, demand that his case be accepted without question?

sentences.zh: 若人皆仕，未知斯事可俟後聖與不？

translations.literal: If all men serve, it is unknown whether this matter may await a later sage or not.
translations.idiomatic: If every man may take office, it is unclear whether this question must wait for a sage of a later age.

sentences.zh: 況仕與不仕，各有其人，而不仕之所引，每感三年之下。

translations.literal: Moreover, serving and not serving each have their men, yet what those who do not serve cite always touches on what lies below the three years of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Serving and refusing office each have their exemplars, yet those who refuse office always appeal to what lies below the full three-year mourning period.

sentences.zh: 見議者弘通情紀，每傍中庸，又云若許譏滕，則恐亡身致命之仕，以此而不盡。

translations.literal: Those who debate broaden feeling and principle and always lean toward the mean, also saying that if Teng may be censured, they fear offices that cost body and life—and on this account do not press the argument to the end.
translations.idiomatic: The debaters broaden feeling and principle and lean toward the middle way; they also say that if Teng may be censured, they fear discouraging men who would give body and life in office—and on that account they stop short of a full verdict.

sentences.zh: 何斯言之過與！

translations.literal: How excessive is this saying!
translations.idiomatic: How far this argument goes!

sentences.zh: 夫忠烈之情，初無計而後動。

translations.literal: Loyal and fierce feeling at first has no calculation and only afterward moves.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal and fierce devotion does not calculate first and act afterward.

sentences.zh: 若計而後動，則懼法不盡命。

translations.literal: If one calculates and then moves, one fears the law and does not exhaust one's life.
translations.idiomatic: If one calculates first, one fears the law and holds back one's life.

sentences.zh: 若有不盡，則國有常法。

translations.literal: If there is failure to exhaust it, the state has its constant law.
translations.idiomatic: If one holds back, the state has its standing law.

sentences.zh: 故古人軍敗於外，而家誅於內。

translations.literal: Therefore the ancients, when the army was defeated abroad, executed the family at home.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the ancients, when armies were defeated abroad, punished the families at home.

sentences.zh: 苟忠發自內，或懼法於外，復有踟躕顧望之地邪！

translations.literal: If loyalty arises from within, or one fears the law without, is there still room to hesitate and look back!
translations.idiomatic: If loyalty springs from within, or one fears the law without, what room is left to hesitate and look back!

sentences.zh: 若有功不賞，有罪不誅，可致斯喻爾。

translations.literal: If merit is not rewarded and guilt is not punished, one may arrive at such a comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Only if merit went unrewarded and guilt unpunished could such a comparison arise.

sentences.zh: 無有名教翼其子弟，而子弟不致力於所天。

translations.literal: There is no case where moral teaching wings a man's sons and younger brothers yet they do not devote themselves to what they look up to.
translations.idiomatic: Never has moral teaching supported a man's sons and younger brothers while they refused to devote themselves to what they owe allegiance.

sentences.zh: 不致力於所天，則王經忠不能救主，孝不顧其親，是家國之罪人爾，何所而稱乎？

translations.literal: If they do not devote themselves to what they look up to, then Wang Jing's loyalty could not save his lord, and filial piety did not care for parents—they are criminals against family and state; what is there to praise?
translations.idiomatic: Without such devotion, Wang Jing's loyalty could not have saved his lord and filial sons would not have cared for their parents—they would be criminals against family and state. What praise could they claim?

sentences.zh: 夫恩宥十世，非不隆也；

translations.literal: Favor extending ten generations is not ungenerous;
translations.idiomatic: Grace extending ten generations is no small bounty;

sentences.zh: 功高賞厚，非不報也。

translations.literal: high merit with thick reward is not unrewarded.
translations.idiomatic: and high merit with rich reward is not left unrequited.

sentences.zh: 若國憲無負於滕恬，則羨之通塞，自是名教之所及，豈是勸沮之本乎？

translations.literal: If the state's constitution owes Teng Tian nothing, then whether Xian is cleared or blocked lies within what moral teaching reaches—how could that be the root of encouragement and deterrence?
translations.idiomatic: If the laws of the state owe Teng Tian no debt, then whether Xian is excused or condemned falls within the reach of moral teaching alone—it cannot be the foundation on which the realm encourages or restrains its subjects.

sentences.zh: 議者又以唐虞邈矣，孰知所歸，尋言求意，將所負者多乎。

translations.literal: The debaters also say that Yao and Shun are remote and none knows where to turn; seeking meaning in their words, perhaps what is owed is the greater part.
translations.idiomatic: The debaters also say that the age of Yao and Shun is far away and none knows where to turn; if one searches their words for intent, perhaps the burden of obligation is greater than we think.

sentences.zh: 後漢亂而不亡，前史猶謂數公之力。

translations.literal: Later Han was chaotic yet did not perish; earlier histories still attribute this to the power of several lords.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han fell into disorder yet did not perish, and earlier histories still credit a few great men for that.

sentences.zh: 魏國將建，荀令君正色異議，董昭不得枕蘇則之膝，賈充受辱於庾純。

translations.literal: When Wei was about to be established, Lord Xun of Ling spoke with stern countenance in dissent; Dong Zhao could not rest his head on Su Ze's knee; Jia Chong was shamed by Yu Chun.
translations.idiomatic: When the state of Wei was about to be founded, Xun Yu spoke out with stern dissent; Dong Zhao could not lean on Su Ze's knee as a confidant; Jia Chong was put to shame by Yu Chun.

sentences.zh: 以此而推，天下之正義，終自傳而不沒，何為發斯歎哉！

translations.literal: Inferring from this, the righteousness of the realm will in the end transmit itself and not perish—why utter such a sigh!
translations.idiomatic: From this one may infer that righteousness in the realm will always be handed on and never die out—why then utter such a sigh of despair!

sentences.zh: 若以時非上皇，便不足復言多者，則夷、齊於奭、望，子房於四人，亦無所復措其言矣。

translations.literal: If because the time is not that of the Highest Sovereign one need no longer speak much, then Bo Yi and Shu Qi toward the Duke of Shao and Taigong Wang, and Zifang toward the Four Elders, would also have nowhere to set their words.
translations.idiomatic: If because the age is not that of the Highest Sovereign one may no longer speak freely, then Bo Yi and Shu Qi before the Duke of Shao and Taigong Wang, and Zhang Liang before the Four Elders of Mount Shang, would also have had no place to speak.

sentences.zh: 至於陳平默順避禍，以權濟屈，皆是衛生免害，非為榮也。

translations.literal: As for Chen Ping's silent compliance and avoidance of disaster, using expedients to relieve constraint—all were to preserve life and escape harm, not for glory.
translations.idiomatic: As for Chen Ping's silent compliance and avoidance of disaster, using expedients to survive hard times—all were to preserve life and escape harm, not for honor.

sentences.zh: 滕今生無所衛，鞭塞已冥，義安在乎？

translations.literal: Teng today has nothing to preserve; the whip and the frontier are already dark—where does righteousness lie?
translations.idiomatic: Teng today has nothing left to preserve; the road to his father's remains is lost in darkness—where then is righteousness?

sentences.zh: 昔陳壽在喪，使婢丸藥，見責鄉閭；

translations.literal: Formerly Chen Shou, while in mourning, had a maid roll pills of medicine and was censured in his village;
translations.idiomatic: In the past Chen Shou, while in mourning, had a maid roll medicine pills and was censured in his home district;

sentences.zh: 阮咸居哀，騎驢偷婢，身處王朝。

translations.literal: Ruan Xian, while dwelling in mourning, rode a donkey and stole a maid, yet stood in the imperial court.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Xian, while mourning, rode a donkey and stole a servant girl, yet still held office at court.

sentences.zh: 豈可以阮獲通於前世，便無疑於後乎！

translations.literal: How can Ruan's being cleared in a former age mean there is no doubt in a later one!
translations.idiomatic: How can the fact that Ruan was excused in an earlier age mean there is no question in a later one!

sentences.zh: 且賢聖抑引，皆是究其始終，定其才行。

translations.literal: Moreover, when sages restrain or promote, they all investigate beginning and end and fix conduct and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: When sages restrain or promote a man, they always weigh his whole course from start to finish and judge his conduct and capacity.

sentences.zh: 故雖事有驚俗，而理必獲申。

translations.literal: Therefore though an affair may startle custom, principle must still be vindicated.
translations.idiomatic: Thus even when an act shocks custom, principle must still be upheld.

sentences.zh: 郗詵葬母後園，而身登宦，所以免責，以其孝也。

translations.literal: Xi Chao buried his mother in the rear garden yet himself entered office; he was excused because of his filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Chao buried his mother in the rear garden yet still took office; he was excused because of his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 日磾殺兒無譏，以其忠也。

translations.literal: Jin Midi killed his son without censure, because of his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Midi killed his son without censure, because of his loyalty to the throne.

sentences.zh: 今豈可以二事是忠孝之所為，便可許殺兒葬母後園乎？

translations.literal: Now can one, because these two affairs are what loyalty and filial piety do, permit killing one's son and burying one's mother in the rear garden?
translations.idiomatic: Can one now, because these two acts were deeds of loyalty and filial piety, permit every man to kill his son or bury his mother in the rear garden?

sentences.zh: 不可明矣。

translations.literal: It cannot be made clear—indeed it cannot.
translations.idiomatic: Clearly it cannot.

sentences.zh: 既其不可，便當究定滕之才行，無所多辯也。

translations.literal: Since it cannot, one should investigate and fix Teng's conduct and capacity, without further debate.
translations.idiomatic: Since it cannot, one should judge Teng's own conduct and capacity, and debate no further.

sentences.zh: 滕非下官鄉親，又不周旋，才能非所能悉。

translations.literal: Teng is not a fellow townsman of this inferior officer, nor have we associated; his talent and capacity are not what I can fully know.
translations.idiomatic: Teng is neither my kinsman nor an acquaintance, and I cannot claim to know his full talent or character.

sentences.zh: 若以滕謀能決敵，才能周用，此自追蹤古人，非議所及。

translations.literal: If by Teng's stratagems he can decide the enemy and his talent and capacity are fully employed, this itself follows the ancients and is beyond what debate can reach.
translations.idiomatic: If Teng's plans can decide battles and his talents are fully employed, that would place him among the ancients and lies beyond the scope of this debate.

sentences.zh: 若是士流，故謂宜如子夏受曾參之詞，可謂善矣，而子夏無不孝之稱也。

translations.literal: If he is of the gentry stream, I therefore say he ought, like Zixia receiving Zeng Shen's rebuke, to be called good—yet Zixia bears no name of unfilial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: If he is an ordinary gentleman, he ought, like Zixia accepting Zeng Shen's rebuke, to be judged favorably—yet Zixia was never called unfilial.

sentences.zh: 意之所懷，都盡於此，自非名理，何緣多其往復；

translations.literal: What the heart holds is all exhausted here; unless it concerns doctrine and principle, why multiply back-and-forth;
translations.idiomatic: What I mean to say is all here; unless the question is one of doctrine and principle, why multiply exchanges;

sentences.zh: 如其折中，裁之居宗。

translations.literal: if one splits the difference, let judgment rest with the chief.
translations.idiomatic: if a middle way is sought, let the chief among you decide.

sentences.zh: 桓偉進號安西，轉補功曹，舉陳郡謝絢自代，曰：「蓋聞知賢弗推，臧文所以竊位；

translations.literal: Huan Wei was advanced to the title Anxi, transferred and appointed Registrar of Achievements, and recommended Xie Xuan of Chen commandery to replace himself, saying: 'I have heard that knowing the worthy yet not recommending him is why Zang Wen usurped his post;
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wei was promoted to the title Anxi, transferred to serve as Registrar of Achievements, and recommended Xie Xuan of Chen commandery to succeed him, saying: 'I have heard that to know a worthy man and not recommend him is how Zang Wen kept a post he did not deserve;

sentences.zh: 宣子能讓，晉國以之獲寧。

translations.literal: Xuanzi was able to yield, and the State of Jin thereby obtained peace.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xuanzi knew how to yield, Jin was restored to stability.

sentences.zh: 鮮之猥承人乏，謬蒙過眷，既恩以義隆，遂再叨非服。

translations.literal: Xianzhi basely inherited others' lack, mistakenly received excessive favor, and since grace had been raised by righteousness, he again usurped an unsuitable post.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi humbly acknowledged that he had inherited a position others lacked the strength to fill; by mistaken excessive favor his obligations had grown beyond merit, and he had twice accepted office unworthy of him.

sentences.zh: 知進之難，屢以上請，然自退之志，未獲暫申，夙夜懷冰，敢忘其懼。

translations.literal: Knowing the difficulty of advancement, he repeatedly submitted requests upward, yet his will to withdraw himself had not briefly been expressed; day and night he harbored ice and did not dare forget his fear.
translations.idiomatic: He knew how hard it was to advance and had petitioned repeatedly to step aside, yet had never been allowed to resign; night and day he trembled with dread and did not dare forget his anxiety.

sentences.zh: 伏見行參軍謝絢，清悟審正，理懷通美，居以端右，雖未足舒其采章，升庸以漸，差可以位擬人。

translations.literal: I humbly observe Staff Administrator Xie Xuan: clear in understanding, careful and upright, his principles and sentiments broadly excellent; placed in a commanding position, although insufficient to unfold his brilliance fully, promoted by gradual steps he could roughly be matched to the post by the man.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully recommend Staff Administrator Xie Xuan — intelligent, discerning, upright, and broadly accomplished in mind and principle. Though a senior post might not yet fully display his talents, gradual promotion would make him a fitting match for the office.

sentences.zh: 請乞愚短，甘充下列，授為賢牧，實副群望。」

translations.literal: I request to beg my own folly and shortcoming, gladly filling the lower rank, appointing him as worthy shepherd — truly fulfilling the multitude's expectation.
translations.idiomatic: I ask to yield my own limited abilities and accept a lesser position instead, and to install him as a capable governor — this would truly meet the public's hopes.

sentences.zh: 入為員外散騎侍郎，司徒左西屬，大司馬琅邪王錄事參軍，仍遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: He entered as Supernumerary Master of Writing for the Dispersed Cavalry, left western subordinate of the Minister over Masses, recording affairs adjutant under the Grand Marshal, Prince of Langye, and was then transferred to Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Supernumerary Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry, Left Western Subordinate of the Minister of Education, and Recording Secretary to the Grand Marshal, the Prince of Langye, before being promoted to Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 性剛直，不阿強貴，明憲直繩，甚得司直之體。

translations.literal: His nature was firm and straight; he did not flatter the powerful and noble; he clarified statutes and held the straight cord — very much obtaining the substance of the censor's integrity.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was upright and unyielding, never currying favor with the mighty; he enforced the law impartially and embodied the true role of a censor.

sentences.zh: 外甥劉毅，權重當時，朝野莫不歸附，鮮之盡心高祖，獨不屈意於毅，毅甚恨焉。

translations.literal: His nephew-in-law Liu Yi held weighty power at the time; court and countryside none did not submit to him. Xianzhi devoted his heart to Emperor Gaozu and alone did not bend his will to Yi — Yi greatly resented this.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Liu Yi wielded immense authority, and everyone in and out of court deferred to him. Xianzhi served Emperor Gaozu loyally and alone refused to defer to Liu Yi, who deeply resented him.

sentences.zh: 義熙六年，鮮之使治書侍御史丘洹奏彈毅曰：「上言傳詔羅道盛輒開箋，遂盜發密事，依法棄市，奏報行刑，而毅以道盛身有侯爵，輒復停宥。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yixi, Xianzhi had Palace Secretary Attendant Imperial Censor Qiu Huan memorialize and impeach Yi, saying: "It was reported upward that the transmission-order bearer Luo Daosheng opened a document case without authorization, thereby stealing and exposing secret affairs; by law he should be executed in the marketplace; the memorial was approved and execution was to proceed, yet Yi, because Daosheng personally held a marquis's rank, again stayed and pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yixi, Xianzhi had the palace secretary and attendant censor Qiu Huan submit an impeachment of Liu Yi, stating: "It was reported that the edict courier Luo Daosheng had opened sealed documents without authorization and disclosed secret state business. By law he should have been executed in public; the memorial was approved and the sentence was to be carried out, yet Yi, because Daosheng held a marquisate in his own right, again intervened and granted him a reprieve.

sentences.zh: 按毅勳德光重，任居次相，既殺之非己，無緣生之自由。

translations.literal: According to the impeachment, Yi's merit and virtue shine with great weight, and his office ranks as the next chancellor; since the execution was not at his hand, he had no grounds to freely grant life.
translations.idiomatic: The charge notes that Liu Yi's merit and standing are great and that he ranks as the second minister of state; since the execution was not his to order, he had no authority to grant life at his own discretion.

sentences.zh: 又奏之於先，而弗請於後，閫外出疆，非此之謂。

translations.literal: Also, he reported this beforehand but did not request afterward — "going outside the women's quarters and crossing the frontier" does not mean this.
translations.idiomatic: He reported the matter in advance but did not seek approval afterward — this is not what is meant by a minister acting beyond his proper authority at home and abroad.

sentences.zh: 中丞鮮之於毅舅甥，制不相糾，臣請免毅官。」

translations.literal: Imperial Censor Xianzhi and Yi are uncle and nephew by marriage; the regulations do not permit mutual impeachment. Your subject requests that Yi's office be removed."
translations.idiomatic: As Xianzhi and Liu Yi are uncle and nephew, regulations forbid them from impeaching one another; I therefore ask that Liu Yi be dismissed from office."

sentences.zh: 詔無所問。

translations.literal: An edict issued saying no inquiry would be made.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict was issued and no action was taken.

sentences.zh: 時新制長吏以父母疾去官，禁錮三年。

translations.literal: At that time a new regulation held that chief officials who left office due to parents' illness would be barred from office for three years.
translations.idiomatic: A new regulation then required that senior officials who resigned because of a parent's illness be barred from holding office for three years.

sentences.zh: 山陰令沈叔任父疾去職，鮮之因此上議曰：「夫事有相權，故制有與奪，此有所屈，而彼有所申。

translations.literal: Shanyin Magistrate Shen Shuren left his post owing to his father's illness. Because of this Xianzhi submitted a memorial saying: "Affairs have mutual weighing, therefore regulations have granting and taking away; here something is bent, there something is expressed.
translations.idiomatic: When Shanyin Magistrate Shen Shuren left office because of his father's illness, Xianzhi submitted a memorial arguing: "Affairs must be weighed against one another, and regulations must allow for both restriction and release — one side may be constrained so that another may be upheld.

sentences.zh: 未有理無所明，事無所獲，而為永制者也。

translations.literal: There is no principle that is not clarified, no affair that gains nothing, yet is made a permanent regulation.
translations.idiomatic: No principle should remain unclear and no policy should yield no benefit, yet still be made a permanent rule.

sentences.zh: 當以去官之人，或容詭託之事。

translations.literal: Perhaps the persons who leave office may accommodate fraudulent pretext affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The concern may be that some who leave office could use illness as a false pretext.

sentences.zh: 詭託之事，誠或有之，豈可虧天下之大教，以末傷本者乎？

translations.literal: Fraudulent pretext affairs — truly there may be such cases; yet how could one impair the great teaching of All under Heaven because of a minor injury to the root?
translations.idiomatic: Such fraud may indeed occur on occasion, but how can we damage the great moral teaching of the realm because of a minor abuse at the margins?

sentences.zh: 且設法蓋以眾苞寡，而不以寡違眾，況防杜去官而塞孝愛之實。

translations.literal: Moreover, establishing laws generally wraps the many around the few, and does not use the few to violate the many; how much more when preventing those who leave office blocks the reality of filial love.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, laws are made to protect the many rather than let the few override the many — all the more so when blocking resignation also blocks the genuine practice of filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 且人情趨於榮利，辭官本非所防，所以為其制者，蒞官不久，則奔競互生，故杜其欲速之情，以申考績之實。

translations.literal: Moreover, human feelings tend toward glory and profit; leaving office in itself is not what should be guarded against. What the regulation guards is: if one holds office not long, then scrambling and rivalry mutually arise — therefore block their haste, to express the reality of performance evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, people naturally pursue honor and profit; resignation itself is not what needs guarding against. The rule exists because those who take office briefly and leave quickly breed factional scrambling — the aim is to curb haste and uphold genuine performance review.

sentences.zh: 省父母之疾，而加以罪名，悖義疾理，莫此為大。

translations.literal: To see parents' illness yet add a criminal charge — contrary to righteousness and harsh to principle; nothing is greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: To visit a sick parent and be punished for it is the greatest possible violation of both righteousness and reason.

sentences.zh: 謂宜從舊，於義為允。」

translations.literal: I say it is fitting to follow the old practice; in righteousness this is acceptable."
translations.idiomatic: The former practice should be restored — that would be the right course."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: They followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his recommendation.

sentences.zh: 於是自二品以上父母沒者，墳墓崩毀及疾病族屬輒去，並不禁錮。

translations.literal: Thereupon from the second rank upward, those whose parents died, whose graves collapsed and were ruined, or whose clansmen fell ill and who immediately left — all were not barred from office.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter officials of the second rank and above who left office upon a parent's death, because graves had fallen into ruin, or because of illness among close relatives were no longer subject to the three-year ban.

sentences.zh: 劉毅當鎮江陵，高祖會於江寧，朝士畢集。

translations.literal: Liu Yi was about to be stationed at Jiangling; Emperor Gaozu met him at Jiangning; court gentlemen all assembled.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yi was about to take up his post at Jiangling, Emperor Gaozu met him at Jiangning, and the entire court gathered.

sentences.zh: 毅素好摴蒱，於是會戲。

translations.literal: Yi had always loved dice gambling; thereupon they played at the assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi had always loved dice games, and so they began to play at the gathering.

sentences.zh: 高祖與毅斂局，各得其半，積錢隱人，毅呼高祖並之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu and Yi collected the board — each getting half; they piled money and a person hid it. Yi called for Emperor Gaozu to join his pile.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu and Liu Yi gathered the dice board and split the stakes evenly; they heaped up the coins and had someone cover them, then Liu Yi invited the emperor to combine his wager with his own.

sentences.zh: 先擲得雉，高祖甚不說，良久乃答之。

translations.literal: First toss got "phoenix" — Emperor Gaozu was very displeased; after a long while he answered it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi rolled first and scored a winning "phoenix" combination; Emperor Gaozu was deeply displeased and only after a long pause did he respond in kind.

sentences.zh: 四坐傾矚，既擲，五子盡黑，毅意色大惡，謂高祖曰：「知公不以大坐席與人！」

translations.literal: The whole assembly leaned and gazed; when the toss was done, all five dice were black; Yi's expression greatly worsened; he said to Emperor Gaozu: "I know you would not give the great seat at the table to another!"
translations.idiomatic: The whole assembly watched intently; when the dice fell, all five showed black — Liu Yi's face darkened with dismay, and he said to Emperor Gaozu, "I knew you would never yield the winning hand to anyone else!"

sentences.zh: 鮮之大喜，徒跣繞床大叫，聲聲相續。

translations.literal: Xianzhi was greatly delighted; barefoot he circled the bed shouting, shout after shout in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi was overjoyed; he ran barefoot around the gaming table shouting again and again without stopping.

sentences.zh: 毅甚不平，謂之曰：「此鄭君何為者！」

translations.literal: Yi was very discontent; he said to him: "What is this Lord Zheng doing!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi was furious and said to him, "What do you think you're doing, Lord Zheng!"

sentences.zh: 無復甥舅之禮。

translations.literal: No longer was there nephew-and-uncle courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: From that point on, all uncle-and-nephew decorum between them was gone.

sentences.zh: 高祖少事戎旅，不經涉學，及為宰相，頗慕風流，時或言論，人皆依違之，不敢難也。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu had early been in military campaigns and had not passed through learning; when he became Chancellor he greatly admired refined culture; at times he would discuss — everyone accommodated him and did not dare object.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu had spent his youth in military service and had little formal education; once he became chancellor he came to admire literary culture, and when he held forth on occasion everyone humored him and no one dared contradict him.

sentences.zh: 鮮之難必切至，未嘗寬假，要須高祖辭窮理屈，然後置之。

translations.literal: Xianzhi's objections were always incisive; he never showed leniency — he required that Emperor Gaozu exhaust his words and be defeated in principle before he would let the matter drop.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi's challenges were always sharp and uncompromising; he would not let a topic rest until Emperor Gaozu had talked himself out and been refuted on the merits.

sentences.zh: 高祖或有時慚恧，變色動容，既而謂人曰：「我本無術學，言義尤淺。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu would sometimes feel ashamed, change color and move his countenance, and afterward say to people: "I originally had no scholarly art; in discussing righteousness I am especially shallow.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu would sometimes flush with embarrassment and change expression, and afterward tell others, "I have no real learning to speak of, and my grasp of moral principle is especially shallow.

sentences.zh: 比時言論，諸賢多見寬容，唯鄭不爾，獨能盡人之意，甚以此感之。」

translations.literal: In discussions at that time, many worthies showed me tolerance; only Zheng did not — he alone could fully express people's meaning; I deeply feel moved by this."
translations.idiomatic: In those discussions most of the worthies indulged me, but Zheng alone did not — he alone spoke what others truly thought, and I am deeply moved by that."

sentences.zh: 時人謂為「格佞」。

translations.literal: People of the time called this "Checking the Flatterers."
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries nicknamed him "the Flatterer-Checker."

sentences.zh: 自中丞轉司徒左長史，太尉諮議參軍，俄而補侍中，復為太尉諮議。

translations.literal: From Imperial Censor he transferred to Left Chief of the Minister over Masses, Counselor Attendant of the Grand Marshal; shortly afterward he was appointed Attending Palace Gentleman, again Grand Marshal Counselor Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He moved from imperial censor to left chief administrator under the Minister of Education and counselor-attendant to the Grand Marshal; soon afterward he was appointed attendant-in-ordinary and again served as counselor to the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 十二年，高祖北伐，以為右長史。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Emperor Gaozu marched north; he was made Right Chief Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, when Emperor Gaozu launched his northern campaign, Xianzhi was appointed right chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 鮮之曾祖墓在開封，相去三百里，乞求拜省，高祖以騎送之。

translations.literal: Xianzhi's great-grandfather's tomb was at Kaifeng, three hundred li distant; he requested leave to visit and pay respects; Emperor Gaozu sent him off by mounted escort.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi's great-grandfather was buried at Kaifeng, three hundred li away; he asked permission to visit the tomb, and Emperor Gaozu provided a mounted escort for the journey.

sentences.zh: 宋國初建，轉奉常。

translations.literal: When the Song state was first established, he transferred to Director of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song state was first founded, he was appointed director of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 佛佛虜陷關中，高祖復欲北討，行意甚盛。

translations.literal: The Fofo barbarians captured Guanzhong; Emperor Gaozu again wished to campaign north; his intent was very strong.
translations.idiomatic: After the Northern Wei captured Guanzhong, Emperor Gaozu again wanted to mount a northern expedition, and his resolve was very firm.

sentences.zh: 鮮之上表諫曰：「伏思聖略深遠，臣之愚管無所措其意。

translations.literal: Xianzhi submitted a memorial remonstrating: "I humbly reflect — the sacred strategy is deep and far; your servant's foolish narrowness has nowhere to place its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying: "I reflect that Your Majesty's strategic vision is profound and far-reaching, and my limited understanding can scarcely grasp its intent.

sentences.zh: 然臣愚見，竊有所懷。

translations.literal: Yet your servant's foolish view — I secretly have something in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in my humble opinion I do have private concerns to offer.

sentences.zh: 虜凶狡情狀可見，自關中再敗，皆是帥師違律，非是內有事故，致外有敗傷。

translations.literal: The barbarians' fierce and cunning disposition can be seen; since the second defeat in Guanzhong, all were because commanding generals violated regulations — not because within there was internal incident causing external defeat and injury.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy's ferocity and cunning are plain to see; the repeated defeats in Guanzhong were all due to commanders violating military discipline, not to internal disorder causing external disaster.

sentences.zh: 虜聞殿下親御六軍，必謂見伐，當重兵守潼關，其勢然也。

translations.literal: The barbarians, hearing Your Highness personally commands the Six Armies, will surely say they see invasion; they will heavily guard Tong Pass — this trend is so.
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy hears that Your Highness will personally lead the Six Armies, they will surely take it as a full-scale invasion and concentrate heavy forces at Tong Pass — that is the natural course of events.

sentences.zh: 若陵威長驅，臣實見其未易；

translations.literal: If we display majesty and drive straight in, your servant truly sees it is not easy;
translations.idiomatic: If we press forward in full force, I frankly do not see how that can succeed easily;

sentences.zh: 若輿駕頓洛，則不足上勞聖躬。

translations.literal: If the imperial carriage halts at Luoyang, then it is insufficient to vex the sacred person above.
translations.idiomatic: If the imperial carriage stops at Luoyang, the gain would not justify troubling Your Majesty in person.

sentences.zh: 如此，則進退之機，宜在熟慮。

translations.literal: Thus, the opportunity to advance or retreat — it is fitting to consider thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Under these circumstances, the decision to advance or hold back ought to be weighed with the utmost care.

sentences.zh: 賊不敢乘勝過陝，遠懾大威故也。

translations.literal: The bandits dared not take advantage of victory to cross Shan — far awed by great majesty for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy did not dare press their advantage beyond Shan precisely because they were held in awe by Your Majesty's formidable presence.

sentences.zh: 今盡用兵之算，事從屈申，遣師撲討，而南夏清晏，賊方懼將來，永不敢動。

translations.literal: Now exhaust the calculations of using troops; let affairs follow bending and extending; dispatch armies to strike down — then South Xia is clear and peaceful; the bandits then fear what is coming and will forever not dare move.
translations.idiomatic: If we now deploy our full military resources with flexible strategy and send armies to suppress the enemy, the south will remain tranquil; the foe will fear what is to come and will never dare stir again.

sentences.zh: 若輿駕造洛而反，凶醜更生揣量之心，必啟邊戎之患，此既必然。

translations.literal: If the imperial carriage goes to Luoyang and returns, the vicious villains again engender thoughts of weighing odds; they will surely open border garrison calamity — this is already inevitable.
translations.idiomatic: If the imperial procession goes to Luoyang and then withdraws, the enemy will again begin calculating their chances and border troubles will surely follow — that much is certain.

sentences.zh: 江南顒顒，傾注輿駕，忽聞遠伐，不測師之深淺，必以殿下大申威靈，未還，人情恐懼，事又可推。

translations.literal: South of the Yangtze all look up expectantly, fixed on the imperial carriage; suddenly hearing of a distant expedition, unable to gauge the depth or shallowness of the army — they will surely say Your Highness greatly displays awesome spirit; not yet returned, popular feeling will fear — the matter can also be inferred.
translations.idiomatic: All south of the Yangtze look to the throne with eager expectation; if they suddenly hear of a distant campaign and cannot tell how large the army is, they will assume Your Highness is projecting full imperial might — and if you do not return promptly, public fear is easy to foresee.

sentences.zh: 往年西征，劉鍾危殆，前年劫盜破廣州，人士都盡。

translations.literal: In past years on the western expedition, Liu Zhong was in peril; the year before robbers plundered and broke Guangzhou — gentlemen were all exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: In the western campaign of years past Liu Zhong was nearly destroyed; the year before last bandits sacked Guangzhou and the gentry were utterly ruined.

sentences.zh: 三吳心腹之內，諸縣屢敗，皆由勞役所致。

translations.literal: Within the heartland of the Three Wus, various counties repeatedly defeated — all caused by corvee labor.
translations.idiomatic: Within the heartland of the Three Wu regions, county after county has suffered unrest — all because of the burden of corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 又聞處處大水，加遠師民敝，敗散，自然之理。

translations.literal: Also I hear everywhere great floods; add distant expedition and people weariness — defeat and scattering is natural principle.
translations.idiomatic: I also hear of flooding everywhere; combined with the strain of a distant campaign on an exhausted populace, collapse and dispersal would be the natural outcome.

sentences.zh: 殿下在彭城，劫盜破諸縣，事非偶爾，皆是無賴凶慝。

translations.literal: When Your Highness was at Pengcheng, robbers broke various counties — the affair was not occasional; all were rascals and vicious wicked ones.
translations.idiomatic: While Your Highness was at Pengcheng, bandits ravaged one county after another — this was no isolated incident but the work of desperate and vicious men.

sentences.zh: 凡順而撫之，則百姓思安；

translations.literal: Whenever one follows and comforts them, then the hundred surnames think of peace;
translations.idiomatic: If they are treated with understanding and care, the common people will seek peace;

sentences.zh: 違其所願，必為亂矣。

translations.literal: Violate what they desire, they will surely become disorderly.
translations.idiomatic: but if their wishes are thwarted, rebellion will surely follow.

sentences.zh: 古人所以救其煩穢，正在於斯。

translations.literal: The ancients' reason for relieving such troubles and filth lies precisely in this.
translations.idiomatic: This is precisely why the ancients sought to relieve such burdens and disorders.

sentences.zh: 漢高身困平城，呂后受匈奴之辱，魏武軍敗赤壁，宣武喪師枋頭，神武之功，一無所損。

translations.literal: Han Gaozu personally was trapped at Pingcheng; Empress Lü received the Xiongnu humiliation; Wei Wu's army was defeated at Red Cliffs; Emperor Xuanwu lost his army at Fangtou — their divine martial merit, not one point was diminished.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu of Han was besieged at Pingcheng and Empress Lü suffered the humiliation of the Xiongnu; Cao Cao was defeated at Red Cliffs and Emperor Xuanwu of Jin lost his army at Fangtou — yet none of these setbacks diminished their imperial stature in the least.

sentences.zh: 況偏師失律，無虧於廟堂之上者邪！

translations.literal: Moreover a detached army lost discipline — what loss to the imperial court above?
translations.idiomatic: How much less should a partial defeat by a subordinate army diminish the throne itself!

sentences.zh: 即之事實，非敗之謂，唯齡石等可念爾。

translations.literal: Viewing the actual facts — it is not called defeat; only Ling Shi and the others are to be lamented.
translations.idiomatic: Judging by the actual facts, this was not truly a defeat — only Zhu Lingshi and his fellows are to be mourned.

sentences.zh: 若行也，或速其禍。

translations.literal: If you march, perhaps you will hasten the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: If you proceed, you may only hasten disaster.

sentences.zh: 反覆思惟，愚謂不煩殿下親征小劫。

translations.literal: Turning it over and thinking — I foolishly say there is no need for Your Highness personally to campaign against a small bandit.
translations.idiomatic: After careful reflection, I humbly submit that Your Highness need not personally campaign against so minor a foe.

sentences.zh: 西虜或為河、洛之患，今正宜通好北虜，則河南安。

translations.literal: Western barbarians may become a He-Luo calamity; now it is precisely fitting to open good relations with the northern barbarians — then Henan is secure.
translations.idiomatic: The western enemy may yet threaten the Yellow and Luo river region; the proper course now is to seek good relations with the northern barbarians, so that Henan may be secured.

sentences.zh: 河南安，則濟、泗靜。

translations.literal: When Henan is secure, then Ji and Si are quiet.
translations.idiomatic: Once Henan is secure, the Ji and Si regions will be at peace.

sentences.zh: 伏願聖鑒察臣愚懷。」

translations.literal: I humbly wish the sacred mirror to examine your servant's foolish thoughts."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg Your Majesty to consider these humble concerns of mine."

sentences.zh: 高祖踐阼，遷太常，都官尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, Xianzhi was transferred to Grand Master of Ceremonies, Director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne, Xianzhi was appointed grand master of ceremonies and director of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 鮮之為人通率，在高祖坐，言無所隱，時人甚憚焉。

translations.literal: Xianzhi as a person was open and straightforward; in Emperor Gaozu's presence his words had nothing hidden — people of the time greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi was by nature frank and unreserved; in Emperor Gaozu's presence he spoke without concealment, and people of the day greatly feared him.

sentences.zh: 而隱厚篤實，贍恤親故。

translations.literal: Yet privately he was generous and solidly sincere, supporting and comforting kin and old friends.
translations.idiomatic: In private, however, he was warm, steadfast, and generous in supporting relatives and old friends.

sentences.zh: 性好遊行，命駕或不知所適，隨御者所之。

translations.literal: His nature loved roaming; when he ordered his carriage he sometimes did not know where — wherever the attendants went, he followed.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to travel about; when he ordered his carriage out he sometimes had no destination in mind and simply went wherever his attendants drove.

sentences.zh: 尤為高祖所狎，上嘗於內殿宴飲，朝貴畢至，唯不召鮮之。

translations.literal: He was especially favored by Emperor Gaozu. The Emperor once feasted in the inner hall; court nobles all arrived — only Xianzhi was not summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu was especially fond of him. Once the emperor held a banquet in the inner hall and all the court nobles were present — except Xianzhi, who was not invited.

sentences.zh: 坐定，謂群臣曰：「鄭鮮之必當自來。」

translations.literal: When seated, he said to the ministers: "Zheng Xianzhi is sure to come himself."
translations.idiomatic: Once everyone was seated, he told the assembled ministers, "Zheng Xianzhi is sure to come on his own."

sentences.zh: 俄而外啟：「尚書鮮之詣神虎門求啟事。」

translations.literal: Shortly a report from outside: "Director Xianzhi has come to Shenhu Gate requesting to enter on business."
translations.idiomatic: Before long a report came from outside: "Director Xianzhi has arrived at Shenhu Gate seeking an audience."

sentences.zh: 高祖大笑引入，其被親遇如此。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu laughed greatly and had him brought in — he was favored to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu laughed heartily and had him admitted — such was the degree of favor he enjoyed.

sentences.zh: 永初二年，出為丹陽尹，復入為都官尚書，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongchu, he went out as Governor of Danyang; again entered as Director of the Ministry of Justice, with additional title Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongchu he was sent out as governor of Danyang, then recalled as director of the Ministry of Justice with the additional title of regular attendant of the dispersed cavalry.

sentences.zh: 以從征功，封龍陽縣五等子。

translations.literal: For merit in following the campaign, he was enfeoffed as Fifth-rank Viscount of Longyang.
translations.idiomatic: For his service on the northern campaign he was enfeoffed as fifth-rank viscount of Longyang County.

sentences.zh: 出為豫章太守，秩中二千石。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Yuzhang, rank mid-two-thousand-dan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed governor of Yuzhang at the rank of mid-two-thousand-dan.

sentences.zh: 元嘉三年，王弘入為相，舉鮮之為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanjia, Wang Hong entered as Chancellor and recommended Xianzhi as Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanjia, when Wang Hong became chancellor, he recommended Xianzhi for the post of right vice director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒，時年六十四。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died, at age sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year, at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 追贈散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry and Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the titles of regular attendant of the dispersed cavalry and grand master of the palace with golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 文集傳於世。

translations.literal: His collected writings circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings have been handed down to posterity.

sentences.zh: 子愔，位至尚書郎，始興太守。

translations.literal: His son Yin reached the post of Secretariat Gentleman and Governor of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yin rose to the posts of secretariat gentleman and governor of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 裴松之，字世期，河東聞喜人也。

translations.literal: Pei Songzhi, courtesy name Shiji, was a native of Wenxi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi, courtesy name Shiji, was a native of Wenxi in Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖昧，光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Mei was Grand Master for the Brilliant.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Mei served as superintendent of the imperial household.

sentences.zh: 父珪，正員外郎。

translations.literal: His father Gui was Regular Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gui held the post of regular master of writing.

sentences.zh: 松之年八歲，學通《論語》、《毛詩》。

translations.literal: At eight years of age Songzhi had mastered the Analects and Mao Odes.
translations.idiomatic: By the age of eight Songzhi had thoroughly mastered the Analects and the Mao version of the Book of Odes.

sentences.zh: 博覽墳籍，立身簡素。

translations.literal: He broadly read the classics and histories; in conduct he was plain and simple.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in the classics and histories and lived a plain, unadorned life.

sentences.zh: 年二十，拜殿中將軍。

translations.literal: At age twenty he was appointed Palace Gentlemen Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he was appointed commandant of the palace gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 此官直衛左右，晉孝武太元中革選名家以參顧問，始用琅邪王茂之、會稽謝輶，皆南北之望。

translations.literal: This office directly guarded left and right; in the Taiyuan era of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin the selection was reformed to use eminent families for consultation; initially Langye Wang Maozhi and Kuaiji Xie Zhou were used — all luminaries of north and south.
translations.idiomatic: This post served as a direct guard at the emperor's side; during the Taiyuan era of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin the selection was reformed to draw on eminent families for imperial consultation, and the first appointees were Wang Maozhi of Langye and Xie Zhou of Kuaiji — both leading figures of north and south.

sentences.zh: 舅庾楷在江陵，欲得松之西上，除新野太守，以事難不行。

translations.literal: His uncle Yu Kai was at Jiangling and wanted Songzhi to go west; he was appointed Governor of Xinye but because affairs were difficult it did not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Yu Kai was stationed at Jiangling and wanted Songzhi to join him in the west; Songzhi was appointed governor of Xinye, but because of the troubled circumstances the appointment never took effect.

sentences.zh: 拜員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Supernumerary Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed supernumerary attendant of the dispersed cavalry.

sentences.zh: 義熙初，為吳興故鄣令，在縣有績。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yixi he was Magistrate of Guchang in Wuxing; in the county he had achievements.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yixi era he served as magistrate of Guchang in Wuxing commandery, where he achieved a notable record of governance.

sentences.zh: 入為尚書祠部郎。

translations.literal: He entered as Gentleman of the Imperial Secretariat in the section for sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as gentleman of the Imperial Secretariat in the section for sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 松之以世立私碑，有乖事實，上表陳之曰：「碑銘之作，以明示後昆，自非殊功異德，無以允應茲典。

translations.literal: Songzhi, because the age established private steles contrary to fact, submitted a memorial stating: "The writing of stele inscriptions is to clearly show posterity; unless there are extraordinary merit and distinctive virtue, one cannot properly respond to this canon.
translations.idiomatic: Because private steles were being erected in his day in ways that distorted the facts, Songzhi submitted a memorial stating: "Stele inscriptions are meant to instruct posterity clearly; unless a man has performed extraordinary service or possessed exceptional virtue, he does not qualify for such an honor.

sentences.zh: 大者道勳光遠，世所宗推；

translations.literal: The greater — the Way's achievements shine far and the age honors and promotes them;
translations.idiomatic: At the highest level are those whose achievements in the Way shine far and whom the age honors and upholds;

sentences.zh: 其次節行高妙，遺烈可紀。

translations.literal: The next — conduct and integrity lofty and subtle, lasting deeds worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: next are those of lofty character and conduct whose lasting legacy deserves to be recorded.

sentences.zh: 若乃亮采登庸，績用顯著，敷化所蒞，惠訓融遠，述詠所寄，有賴鐫勒，非斯族也，則幾乎僭黷矣。

translations.literal: If one merely displays talent and ascends office, achievement and utility prominent, transforming where one governs, gentle instruction merging far — recitations and hymns entrusted — reliant on carving and inscription, if not of this class, then it nearly approaches presumptuous offense.
translations.idiomatic: If one merely displays talent in office, achieves visible results in governance, and spreads benevolent instruction far and wide, yet relies on carved inscriptions to preserve one's praise — when such a person does not belong to either of these categories, the practice comes close to presumptuous overreach.

sentences.zh: 俗敝偽興，華煩已久，是以孔悝之銘，行是人非；

translations.literal: Custom's corruption and falsity have risen; florid excess has long endured; therefore Kong Kui's inscription — the deed does not match the person;
translations.idiomatic: Custom has long been corrupt and false, and ostentatious excess has persisted for ages — hence the inscription for Kong Kui, in which the praise did not match the man;

sentences.zh: 蔡邕制文，每有愧色。

translations.literal: When Cai Yong composed such texts, he always wore a look of shame.
translations.idiomatic: Even Cai Yong, when drafting such inscriptions, would flush with shame.

sentences.zh: 而自時厥後，其流彌多，預有臣吏，必為建立，勒銘寡取信之實，刊石成虛偽之常，真假相蒙，殆使合美者不貴，但論其功費，又不可稱。

translations.literal: Yet from that time onward the practice grew ever more numerous; whenever there were officials and clerks in prospect, steles would invariably be erected; inscribing epitaphs seldom sought the substance of truth; carving stone became the routine of falsehood; truth and falsity covered each other, almost causing those who combined beauty not to be prized—yet to discuss only their labor and expense again cannot be commended.
translations.idiomatic: From that time on the custom spread ever wider: whenever an official was expected, people inevitably erected a stele. Inscriptions rarely rested on verified fact; stone-carving became routine pretense, truth and falsehood piled on one another until genuine merit seemed worthless. To speak only of the cost and labor involved would be equally unflattering.

sentences.zh: 不加禁裁，其敝無已。」

translations.literal: If prohibition and restraint are not applied, the harm will have no end."
translations.idiomatic: Without prohibition, the abuse would never cease."

sentences.zh: 以為「諸欲立碑者，宜悉令言上，為朝議所許，然後聽之。

translations.literal: 」 It was proposed that 「all who wish to erect steles should in every case be made to report upward; only after approval by court deliberation should it be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that anyone wishing to erect a stele must first petition the throne and receive court approval before proceeding.

sentences.zh: 庶可以防遏無徵，顯彰茂實，使百世之下，知其不虛，則義信於仰止，道孚於來葉。」

translations.literal: Thus one might prevent and check the unsubstantiated, clearly display abundant substance, cause those a hundred generations hence to know they are not empty—then righteousness would be trusted in what is revered, and the Way would be received in generations to come.
translations.idiomatic: In this way unsubstantiated praise could be blocked, genuine achievement clearly honored, and future generations assured that what was carved in stone was no lie—so that faith in worthy example would endure and the Way inspire ages yet to come.

sentences.zh: 由是並斷。

translations.literal: 」 Thereupon all were forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: On this basis, the practice of erecting steles was banned entirely.

sentences.zh: 高祖北伐，領司州刺史，以松之為州主簿，轉治中從事史。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor marched north, he held the post of Governor of Sizhou and appointed Songzhi as the prefecture's chief clerk, then transferred him to Registrar and Attendant Official.
translations.idiomatic: During the Founding Emperor's northern campaign, he also served as governor of Sizhou, appointing Songzhi chief clerk of the province and later promoting him to registrar and attendant official.

sentences.zh: 既克洛陽，高祖敕之曰：「裴松之廊廟之才，不宜久尸邊務，今召為世子洗馬，與殷景仁同，可令知之。」

translations.literal: After Luoyang was taken, the Founding Emperor ordered: 「Pei Songzhi has talent for state council; he should not long occupy himself with frontier duties. Now summon him as Groom-in-Waiting to the Heir Apparent, together with Yin Jingren—let him be informed.
translations.idiomatic: After Luoyang fell, the Founding Emperor issued orders: "Pei Songzhi possesses the caliber of a statesman and should not remain tied to frontier affairs. Summon him to serve as Groom-in-Waiting to the Heir Apparent alongside Yin Jingren, and inform him accordingly."

sentences.zh: 於時議立五廟樂，松之以妃臧氏廟樂亦宜與四廟同。

translations.literal: 」 At that time there was discussion of establishing music for the five temples; Songzhi held that the music for Lady Zang's temple should likewise be the same as for the four temples.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated establishing music for the five ancestral temples, Songzhi argued that the music honoring Lady Zang's shrine should match that of the four principal temples.

sentences.zh: 除零陵內史，徵為國子博士。

translations.literal: He was appointed Interior Administrator of Lingling and summoned as Erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed interior administrator of Lingling, then recalled to serve as erudite at the National University.

sentences.zh: 太祖元嘉三年，誅司徒徐羨之等，分遣大使，巡行天下。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanjia under Emperor Taizu, after executing Grand Secretary Xu Xianzhi and others, he dispatched envoys in separate groups to inspect the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanjia, after executing Grand Secretary Xu Xianzhi and his co-conspirators, Emperor Wen dispatched imperial commissioners to tour the entire realm.

sentences.zh: 通直散騎常侍袁渝、司徒左司掾孔邈使揚州，尚書三公郎陸子真、起部甄法崇使荊州，員外散騎常侍范雍、司徒主簿龐遵使南兗州，前尚書右丞孔默使南、北二豫州，撫軍參軍王歆之使徐州，冗從僕射車宗使青、兗州，松之使湘州，尚書殿中郎阮長之使雍州，前竟陵太守殷道鸞使益州，員外散騎常侍李耽之使廣州，郎中殷斌使梁州、南秦州，前員外散騎侍郎阮園客使交州，駙馬都尉、奉朝請潘思先使寧州，並兼散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Regular Court Gentleman Yuan Yu and Left Clerk of the Secretariat Kong Miao were sent to Yangzhou; Secretariat Gentleman of the Three Dukes Lu Zizhen and Registry Officer Zhen Fachong to Jingzhou; Supernumerary Regular Court Gentleman Fan Yong and Secretariat Clerk Pang Zun to South Yanzhou; former Right Assistant Director of the Secretariat Kong Mo to South and North Yuzhou; Adjutant to the Pacification General Wang Xinzhi to Xuzhou; Supernumerary Attendant of the Rear Carriage Che Zong to Qingzhou and Yanzhou; Songzhi to Xiangzhou; Palace Attendant in the Secretariat Ruan Changzhi to Yongzhou; former Administrator of Jingling Yin Daoluan to Yizhou; Supernumerary Regular Court Gentleman Li Danzhi to Guangzhou; Gentleman Yin Bin to Liangzhou and South Qinzhou; former Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Cavalry Ruan Yuank to Jiaozhou; Commandant of Cavalry for Imperial Affines and Attendant Pan Sixian to Ningzhou—all also holding the concurrent title of Regular Court Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yu, palace attendant and regular court gentleman, and Kong Miao, left clerk of the grand secretary's office, were sent to Yangzhou; Lu Zizhen of the secretariat and registry officer Zhen Fachong to Jingzhou; Fan Yong and secretariat clerk Pang Zun to South Yanzhou; former assistant director Kong Mo to both Yuzhou provinces; adjutant Wang Xinzhi to Xuzhou; attendant Che Zong to Qing and Yan provinces; Songzhi to Xiangzhou; Ruan Changzhi to Yongzhou; former Jingling prefect Yin Daoluan to Yizhou; Li Danzhi to Guangzhou; Yin Bin to Liang and South Qin provinces; former cavalry attendant Ruan Yuank to Jiaozhou; and Pan Sixian, commandant for imperial affines, to Ningzhou—each also bearing the concurrent rank of regular court gentleman.

sentences.zh: 班宣詔書曰：「昔王者巡功，群后述職，不然則有存省之禮，聘眺之規。

translations.literal: They promulgated and proclaimed the imperial edict, saying: 「Of old the king inspected achievements on tour, and the feudal lords reported on their duties; otherwise there were the rites of preservation and inspection, the regulations of embassies and observation.
translations.idiomatic: They circulated the imperial edict, which read: "In antiquity a true king toured the realm to inspect achievements while his lords reported on their duties; when such tours were not possible, he sent envoys to observe local conditions on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 所以觀民立政，命事考績，上下偕通，遐邇咸被，故能功昭長世，道歷遠年。

translations.literal: By this one observes the people and establishes policy, assigns affairs and examines performance; above and below communicate in harmony, far and near are alike covered—thus achievements can shine through long ages, and the Way endure through distant years.
translations.idiomatic: Through this the ruler observes his people and sets policy, assigns duties and evaluates performance, keeping court and countryside in communication so that all regions benefit—thereby ensuring that his achievements shine through the ages and his Way endures for generations.

sentences.zh: 朕以寡闇，屬承洪業，夤畏在位，昧於治道，夕惕惟憂，如臨淵谷。

translations.literal: I, being deficient and dim, have inherited the great enterprise, reverently fearful in my position, ignorant of the Way of governance, anxious in evening vigil, as though standing on the edge of a deep ravine.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am dull and unworthy, I have inherited this vast empire. I hold office with trembling reverence, still unclear on how best to govern, and lie awake each night in anxiety, as if perched above a chasm.

sentences.zh: 懼國俗陵頹，民風凋偽，眚厲違和，水旱傷業。

translations.literal: I fear the customs of the state declining, the people's morals withered and false, disasters and pestilence at odds with harmony, flood and drought harming livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: I fear national custom is slipping, local morality corrupted, pestilence and disaster disrupting peace, and floods and drought ruining livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 雖躬勤庶事，思弘攸宜，而機務惟殷，顧循多闕，政刑乖謬，未獲具聞。

translations.literal: Although I personally toil at myriad affairs, thinking to extend what is appropriate, yet pressing business is abundant, and in review there are many gaps; government and punishments go awry—I have not been able to learn of all fully.
translations.idiomatic: Though I personally attend to every branch of government and strive to do what is right, affairs of state press incessantly and I miss much in my oversight; wrongs in government and law reach me only piecemeal.

sentences.zh: 豈誠素弗孚，使群心莫盡，納隍之愧，在予一人。

translations.literal: Could it be that sincerity and simplicity do not win trust, causing the hearts of the multitude not to be fully expressed? The shame of falling into the moat rests with me alone.
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps my sincere intent has failed to inspire confidence, and the people's hearts go unheard. The shame of this failure falls on me alone.

sentences.zh: 以歲時多難，王道未壹，卜征之禮，廢而未修，眷被氓庶，無忘欽恤。

translations.literal: Because the years and seasons hold many hardships, the kingly Way is not yet unified, the rite of divining for a tour has been abandoned and not restored—yet I turn to regard the common people and do not forget reverent concern.
translations.idiomatic: Times are hard and the realm not yet fully united; the ancient rite of divining before an imperial tour has fallen into disuse. Yet I have not forgotten my duty of tender concern for the common people.

sentences.zh: 今使兼散騎常侍渝等申令四方，周行郡邑，親見刺史二千石官長，申述至誠，廣詢治要，觀察吏政，訪求民隱，旌舉操行，存問所疾。

translations.literal: Now I send the concurrently appointed Regular Court Gentlemen Yu and others to proclaim orders to the four quarters, travel through commands and districts, personally see the regional inspectors and two-thousand-bushel officials, declare utmost sincerity, broadly inquire into essentials of governance, observe official administration, seek out the people's hidden grievances, commend upright conduct, and inquire after those who are ill.
