translations.idiomatic: I now dispatch Yuan Yu and the other commissioners bearing the rank of regular court gentleman to proclaim this edict throughout the realm, tour every commandery and district, meet personally with regional inspectors and prefects, convey my deepest sincerity, inquire widely into effective governance, scrutinize local administration, uncover hidden grievances, commend worthy conduct, and comfort the sick.

sentences.zh: 禮俗得失，一依周典，每各為書，還具條奏，俾朕昭然，若親覽焉。

translations.literal: The gains and losses of rites and customs should all follow the Zhou canon; each should compose a separate report, and upon return submit itemized memorials, so that I may be clearly informed, as if viewing in person.
translations.idiomatic: On rites and customs, follow the standards of the Zhou; each commissioner shall write a separate report and submit a detailed memorial upon return, so that I may understand conditions as clearly as if I had seen them myself.

sentences.zh: 大夫君子，其各悉心敬事，無惰乃力。

translations.literal: Gentlemen and great officers, each of you should devote your heart and respectfully serve, without slacking your strength.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen of the realm, apply yourselves wholeheartedly to this task and spare no effort.

sentences.zh: 其有咨謀遠圖，謹言中誠，陳之使者，無或隱遺。

translations.literal: If anyone has counsel on distant plans and long-term strategy, let them speak with careful sincerity and present it to the envoys, without concealment or omission.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever has far-sighted counsel or earnest advice should bring it frankly to the commissioners—nothing must be withheld.

sentences.zh: 方將敬納良規，以補其闕。

translations.literal: I am about to respectfully receive good counsel to supplement what is lacking.
translations.idiomatic: I shall welcome good counsel and use it to remedy my failings.

sentences.zh: 勉哉勖之，稱朕意焉。」

translations.literal: Strive and be encouraged—fulfill my intent.」
translations.idiomatic: Take up this charge with vigor and bear out my intentions."

sentences.zh: 松之反使，奏曰：「臣聞天道以下濟光明，君德以廣運為極。

translations.literal: When Songzhi returned from his mission, he memorialized: 「Your servant has heard that the Way of Heaven illumines what lies below, and the virtue of a lord reaches its apex in broad bestowal.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his return, Songzhi submitted a memorial: "Your servant has learned that Heaven's Way sheds light upon all below, and a ruler's virtue finds its fullest expression in benevolence spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 古先哲后，因心溥被，是以文思在躬，則時雍自洽，禮行江漢，而美化斯遠。

translations.literal: Ancient sage-rulers of old, following the heart to spread broadly—thus when literary grace was in their persons, the age harmonized of itself; when rites were practiced in the Jiang and Han, gentle transformation reached far.
translations.idiomatic: The sage-kings of antiquity governed from the heart and showered blessings on all beneath them; when wisdom dwelled in the ruler himself, the realm achieved harmony spontaneously, and as ritual spread even to the Yangtze and Han rivers, culture's refining influence reached the farthest corners.

sentences.zh: 故能垂大哉之休詠，廓造周之盛則。

translations.literal: Thus they could hand down the great hymn of praise and broadly create the glorious norms of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they left behind great songs of praise and established the magnificent patterns of the Zhou dynasty.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下神睿玄通，道契曠代，冕旒華堂，垂心八表。

translations.literal: Humbly considering, Your Majesty is divinely wise and profoundly penetrating, your Way matching across vast ages; beneath the crown in the splendid hall, you extend your mind to the eight directions.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's divine wisdom penetrates all mysteries; your Way matches the greatest rulers of ages past. From the throne in your resplendent hall, your concern reaches to the farthest corners of the realm.

sentences.zh: 咨敬敷之未純，慮明揚之靡暢。

translations.literal: You consult on reverent bestowal not yet being pure, and consider that clear promotion has not been fully achieved.
translations.idiomatic: You worry that your benevolent care has not yet reached every corner, and that worthy men have not yet been fully discovered and elevated.

sentences.zh: 清問下民，哀此鰥寡，渙焉大號，周爰四達。

translations.literal: With clear inquiry you descend to the people, pitying these widowers and orphans; broadly you proclaim the great decree, caring everywhere and reaching the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: With earnest inquiry you reach down to the people and pity the widowed and orphaned; your great proclamation resounds, extending your care to every quarter of the realm.

sentences.zh: 遠猷形於《雅》、《誥》，惠訓播乎遐陬。

translations.literal: Far-reaching plans take form in the Odes and Announcements; gracious instruction spreads to distant corners.
translations.idiomatic: Your far-sighted policies echo the wisdom of the Book of Odes and the Great Announcements, and your benevolent teaching reaches even the remotest regions.

sentences.zh: 是故率土仰詠，重譯咸說，莫不謳吟踴躍，式銘皇風。

translations.literal: Therefore throughout the land all look up and sing; through double translation all rejoice—none fail to chant and leap, inscribing the imperial wind.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the whole realm looks up and sings your praise; even those who speak through double translation rejoice alike—all join in song and celebration, recording the glories of your reign.

sentences.zh: 或有扶老攜幼，稱歡路左，誠由亭毒既流，故忘其自至，千載一時，於是乎在。

translations.literal: Some lead the aged and carry the young, expressing joy by the roadside—truly because nurturing grace had already flowed, they forgot it came of itself; a moment in a thousand years—here it is.
translations.idiomatic: Some, supporting the elderly and leading children, declared their joy by the roadside—for such nourishing grace had touched them that they hardly noticed how naturally it came. A moment that comes once in a thousand years is upon us now.

sentences.zh: 臣謬蒙銓任，忝廁顯列，猥以短乏，思純八表，無以宣暢聖旨，肅明風化，黜陟無序，搜揚寡聞，慚懼屏營，不知所措。

translations.literal: Your servant has wrongly received selection and appointment, unworthily occupying a distinguished rank; basely with my shortness and deficiency, thinking to purify the eight directions, I had no means to expand and clarify the sage decree, to make clear the wind of transformation; promotion and demotion were without order, search and elevation were with little heard; ashamed and fearful, I stood aside in confusion, not knowing what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant, unworthy though I am, was entrusted with this high commission despite my limited abilities. I strove to carry your benevolent intent to every corner of the realm but lacked the power to do so fully; I could neither clarify local customs nor promote or demote officials as merit required. Overwhelmed with shame and anxiety, I scarcely knew how to proceed.

sentences.zh: 奉二十四條，謹隨事為牒。

translations.literal: I present twenty-four articles, respectfully appending separate records for each matter.
translations.idiomatic: I submit twenty-four recommendations, each documented in a separate report according to its subject.

sentences.zh: 伏見癸卯詔書，禮俗得失，一依周典，每各為書，還具條奏。

translations.literal: Humbly viewing the guimao edict: on the gains and losses of rites and customs, all according to the Zhou canon—each to compose a separate book and upon return submit itemized memorials.
translations.idiomatic: As instructed in the guimao edict, regarding rites and customs I have followed the Zhou standards, prepared a separate report on each matter, and shall submit detailed memorials upon my return.

sentences.zh: 謹依事為書以繫之後。」

translations.literal: Respectfully, according to each matter I have composed books and attached them afterward.
translations.idiomatic: I have accordingly prepared separate reports on each matter, which are appended below."

sentences.zh: 松之甚得奉使之議，論者美之。

translations.literal: 」 Songzhi very well fulfilled the purpose of the mission; commentators praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Songzhi's mission was widely judged a success, and commentators praised his performance.

sentences.zh: 轉中書侍郎、司冀二州大中正。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman in Attendance of the Central Secretariat and Grand Rectifier of Sizhou and Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to gentleman of the central secretariat and appointed grand rectifier for Sizhou and Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 上使注陳壽《三國志》，松之鳩集傳記，增廣異聞，既成奏上。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered annotation of Chen Shou's Records of the Three Kingdoms; Songzhi gathered biographies and records, expanded strange hearsay, and when completed submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commissioned him to annotate Chen Shou's Records of the Three Kingdoms. Songzhi collected biographical sources, expanded the narrative with additional material, and presented the finished work to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上善之，曰：「此為不朽矣！」

translations.literal: The Emperor approved it, saying: 「This will be imperishable!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised it, declaring, "This work will never perish!"

sentences.zh: 出為永嘉太守，勤恤百姓，吏民便之。

translations.literal: 」 He went out as Administrator of Yongjia, diligently caring for the people; officials and commoners found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Yongjia, where he devoted himself to the people's welfare; both officials and commoners benefited from his administration.

sentences.zh: 入補通直為常侍，復領二州大中正。

translations.literal: He entered to fill the post of Regular Attendant of Direct Communication, and again supervised the two provinces as Grand Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court as regular attendant for direct communication, he again served as grand rectifier for both provinces.

sentences.zh: 尋出為南琅邪太守。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he went out as Administrator of Southern Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed prefect of Southern Langye.

sentences.zh: 十四年致仕，拜中散大夫，尋領國子博士。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he retired from office, was appointed Grand Master of Enjoyment, and shortly afterward supervised as Erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he retired and was granted the title of grand master of enjoyment; he soon took charge as erudite at the National University.

sentences.zh: 進太中大夫，博士如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand Master of the Palace, continuing as erudite as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand master of the palace while retaining his position as erudite.

sentences.zh: 續何承天國史，未及撰述，二十八年，卒，時年八十。

translations.literal: He continued He Chengtian's National History, but before completing the composition, in the twenty-eighth year he died, aged eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He took up the continuation of He Chengtian's national history but died in the twenty-eighth year, at age eighty, before completing it.

sentences.zh: 子駰，南中郎參軍。

translations.literal: His son Yin was a Staff Member of the Southern Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yin served as staff officer to the southern palace guard.

sentences.zh: 松之所著文論及《晉紀》，駰注司馬遷《史記》，並行於世。

translations.literal: Songzhi's collected essays and Annals of Jin, and Yin's annotation of Sima Qian's Records of the Historian, all circulated in the world together.
translations.idiomatic: Songzhi's essays and Annals of Jin, together with Yin's commentary on Sima Qian's Records of the Grand Historian, all circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 何承天，東海郯人也。

translations.literal: He Chengtian was a native of Tan in Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian was a native of Tan in Donghai commandery.

sentences.zh: 從祖倫，晉右衛將軍。

translations.literal: His father's cousin Lun was Right Guard General of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His father's cousin Lun had served as right guard general under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 承天五歲失父，母徐氏，廣之姊也，聰明博學，故承天幼漸訓議，儒史百家，莫不該覽。

translations.literal: Chengtian lost his father at five; his mother was of the Xu clan, elder sister to Guang, intelligent and broadly learned; thus from youth Chengtian was gradually instructed in discussion; Confucian classics, histories, and the hundred schools—none were not exhaustively perused.
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian lost his father at the age of five. His mother, née Xu—elder sister to Xu Guang—was brilliant and well-read, and from early childhood she tutored him in scholarly discourse. He mastered the Confucian classics, history, and the works of the hundred schools.

sentences.zh: 叔父肹為益陽令，隨肹之官。

translations.literal: His uncle's younger brother Xi was Magistrate of Yiyang; Chengtian followed Xi to his post.
translations.idiomatic: When his uncle Xi became magistrate of Yiyang, Chengtian accompanied him to his post.

sentences.zh: 隆安四年，南蠻校尉桓偉命為參軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Long'an, the Colonel of Southern Man Hun Wei appointed him as Staff Member.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Long'an, Colonel of the Southern Man Hun Wei appointed him to his staff.

sentences.zh: 時殷仲堪、桓玄等互舉兵以向朝廷，承天懼禍難未已，解職還益陽。

translations.literal: At the time Yin Zhongkan, Huan Xuan, and others repeatedly raised troops against the court; Chengtian feared calamity would not cease, resigned his post, and returned to Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin Zhongkan, Huan Xuan, and others repeatedly took up arms against the court, Chengtian, fearing endless turmoil, resigned and returned to Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 義旗初，長沙公陶延壽以為其輔國府參軍，遣通敬於高祖，因除瀏陽令，尋去職還都。

translations.literal: At the start of the Righteous Banner, the Duke of Changsha Tao Yanshou made him Staff Member of his Pacification State Office, sent him to convey respect to the Founding Emperor, and on this basis appointed him Magistrate of Liuyang; shortly he left office and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous armies first rose, Duke Tao Yanshou of Changsha took him onto his staff and sent him to pay respects to the future Founding Emperor. He was briefly appointed magistrate of Liuyang, then resigned and returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 撫軍將軍劉毅鎮姑孰，版為行參軍。

translations.literal: The Pacification General Liu Yi was stationed at Gtu, and by provisional appointment made him Acting Staff Member.
translations.idiomatic: When General Liu Yi was posted at Gtu, he appointed Chengtian acting staff officer.

sentences.zh: 毅嘗出行，而鄢陵縣史陳滿射鳥，箭誤中直帥，雖不傷人，處法棄市。

translations.literal: Yi was once traveling out when Yiling County Clerk Chen Man was shooting birds; an arrow mistakenly struck a chief attendant; although no one was wounded, by law he was sentenced to execution in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Once when Yi was on an outing, Chen Man, a county clerk from Yiling, was shooting birds when an arrow accidentally struck a chief attendant in Yi's retinue. Though no one was injured, the sentence under law was execution in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 承天議曰：「獄貴情斷，疑則從輕。

translations.literal: Chengtian argued: 「In judgments what is prized is deciding according to intent; when in doubt, lean toward leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian argued: "The essence of justice lies in judging intent; when doubt remains, the lighter penalty applies.

sentences.zh: 昔驚漢文帝乘輿馬者，張釋之劾以犯蹕，罪止罰金。

translations.literal: Of old, one who startled Emperor Wen of Han's imperial carriage—Zhang Shizhi impeached him for violating the imperial progress, and the crime stopped at a fine of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago, when someone startled Emperor Wen's carriage horse, Zhang Shizhi prosecuted the offense as a breach of the imperial progress, and the penalty was a fine—nothing more.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 明其無心於驚馬也。

translations.literal: To make clear he had no intent to startle the horse.
translations.idiomatic: Because it was clear he had no intention of startling the horse.

sentences.zh: 故不以乘輿之重，加以異制。

translations.literal: Therefore he did not, because of the weight of the imperial carriage, apply a separate penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the law did not impose a harsher penalty simply because an imperial carriage was involved.

sentences.zh: 今滿意在射鳥，非有心於中人。

translations.literal: Now Man's intent was in shooting birds; he did not deliberately aim at a person.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Man's purpose was to shoot birds; he had no intent to strike anyone.

sentences.zh: 按律過誤傷人，三歲刑，況不傷乎？

translations.literal: According to the code, accidental injury to a person carries three years' punishment—how much less when there is no injury?
translations.idiomatic: Under the code, accidental injury carries a three-year sentence—how much more so when no one was hurt at all?

sentences.zh: 微罰可也。」

translations.literal: A light penalty would suffice.
translations.idiomatic: A minor penalty would suffice."

sentences.zh: 出補宛陵令。

translations.literal: 」 He went out to fill the vacancy as Magistrate of Wanling.
translations.idiomatic: He was next appointed magistrate of Wanling.

sentences.zh: 趙惔為寧蠻校尉、尋陽太守，請為司馬。

translations.literal: Zhao Tan was Colonel Who Pacifies the Man and Administrator of Xunyang; he invited Chengtian as Chief Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Tan served as colonel who pacifies the Man and prefect of Xunyang, he invited Chengtian to serve as his chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 尋去職。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He soon resigned that post.

sentences.zh: 高祖以為太尉行參軍。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor appointed him Acting Staff Member to the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor appointed him acting staff officer to the grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 高祖討劉毅，留諸葛長民為監軍。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor attacked Liu Yi, he left Zhuge Changmin as Army Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor marched against Liu Yi, he left Zhuge Changmin behind as army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 長民密懷異志，劉穆之屏人問承天曰：「公今行濟否云何？」

translations.literal: Changmin secretly harbored a different intent; Liu Muzhi dismissed attendants and asked Chengtian: 「Will the Duke's expedition succeed or not?
translations.idiomatic: Changmin secretly harbored rebellious intentions. Liu Muzhi dismissed all attendants and asked Chengtian, "Will the Duke's campaign succeed?"

sentences.zh: 承天曰：「不憂西不時，別有一慮爾。

translations.literal: 」 Chengtian said: 「I do not worry that the west will not arrive on time—there is another concern.
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian replied, "I do not worry about the western campaign's timing—there is another concern altogether.

sentences.zh: 公昔年自左里還入石頭，甚脫爾，今還，宜加重複。」

translations.literal: The Duke in former years returned from Zuoli and entered Stone City very loosely defended; on returning now, he should redouble precautions.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke returned from Zuoli and entered Jiankang years ago, security was dangerously lax. When he returns this time, precautions must be doubled."

sentences.zh: 穆之曰：「非君不聞此言。

translations.literal: 」 Muzhi said: 「Had it not been for you, I would not have heard these words.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi said, "Without you, I would never have heard this warning.

sentences.zh: 頃日願丹徒劉郎，恐不復可得也。」

translations.literal: For some days now I have hoped for the young lord of Dantu—I fear he may no longer be obtainable.
translations.idiomatic: These past days I have counted on Prince Liu of Dantu—I fear he may no longer be available to us."

sentences.zh: 除太學博士。

translations.literal: 」 He was appointed Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian was appointed erudite at the imperial university.

sentences.zh: 義熙十一年，為世子征虜參軍，轉西中郎中軍參軍，錢唐令。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yixi, he was Staff Member of the Heir Apparent's Expel-Barbarians Command; transferred to Staff Member of the Western Headquarters Central Army, Magistrate of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Yixi he served as staff officer to the heir apparent's expel-barbarians command, then transferred to staff officer under the western headquarters central army and magistrate of Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 高祖在壽陽，宋臺建，召為尚書祠部郎，與傅亮共撰朝儀。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor was at Shouyang and the Song administration was established, Chengtian was summoned as Gentleman of Ceremonies in the Secretariat and together with Fu Liang drafted court protocol.
translations.idiomatic: While the Founding Emperor was at Shouyang and the Song regime was being established, Chengtian was summoned as gentleman of ceremonial affairs in the secretariat, and together with Fu Liang drafted court protocol.

sentences.zh: 永初末，補南臺治書侍御史。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongchu, he filled the post of Supervising Secretary and Attendant Censor of the Southern Office.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yongchu era, he was appointed supervising secretary and attendant censor at the southern censorate.

sentences.zh: 謝晦鎮江陵，請為南蠻長史。

translations.literal: When Xie Hui was stationed at Jiangling, he invited Chengtian as Chief Administrator of the Southern Man.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Hui was posted at Jiangling, he invited Chengtian to serve as chief administrator of the southern barbarian command.

sentences.zh: 時有尹嘉者，家貧，母熊自以身貼錢，為嘉償責。

translations.literal: At the time there was one Yin Jia, whose family was poor; his mother Xiong pledged herself for money to repay Jia's debts.
translations.idiomatic: There was a man named Yin Jia whose family was poor. His mother Xiong had sold herself into bondage to pay his debts.

sentences.zh: 坐不孝當死。

translations.literal: Found guilty of unfilial conduct, he was to die.
translations.idiomatic: Convicted of unfilial conduct, he was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 承天議曰：「被府宣令，普議尹嘉大辟事，稱法吏葛滕籤，母告子不孝，欲殺者許之。

translations.literal: Chengtian argued: 「Having received the prefectural order for general deliberation on Yin Jia's capital offense, it cites the legal clerk Ge Teng's ruling: when a mother accuses her son of unfiliality and wishes to kill him, this is permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian argued: "Under the prefecture's order for general deliberation on Yin Jia's capital case, legal clerk Ge Teng ruled that when a mother accuses her son of unfilial conduct and asks for his death, the law permits it.

sentences.zh: 法云，謂違犯教令，敬恭有虧，父母欲殺，皆許之。

translations.literal: The law states: this means violating and transgressing instruction and orders, with respect and reverence deficient—when parents wish to kill, all such cases are permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The statute applies when a child violates parental instruction and shows deficient respect, and the parents wish him dead—the law permits them to ask for execution.

sentences.zh: 其所告惟取信於所求而許之。

translations.literal: What is reported must rely on belief in what is requested before permission is granted.
translations.idiomatic: The law permits execution only when the parent's accusation accords with what they actually seek.

sentences.zh: 謹尋事原心，嘉母辭自求質錢，為子還責。

translations.literal: Carefully tracing the matter to its root intent: Jia's mother's words were that she herself sought pledged money to repay her son's debts.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the facts in light of the parties' intentions, Jia's mother stated that she had pledged herself for money to repay her son's debts.

sentences.zh: 嘉雖虧犯教義，而熊無請殺之辭。

translations.literal: Although Jia did fall short of violating filial teaching, Xiong had no words requesting his death.
translations.idiomatic: Though Jia had indeed failed in filial duty, Xiong never asked for his death.

sentences.zh: 熊求所以生之而今殺之，非隨所求之謂。

translations.literal: Xiong sought means whereby he could live, yet now he is to be killed—this is not what is meant by following what is requested.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong sought a way for her son to live; to execute him now is not to honor what she asked for.

sentences.zh: 始以不孝為劾，終於和賣結刑，倚旁兩端，母子俱罪，滕籤法文，為非其條。

translations.literal: At first the charge was unfiliality; at the end it rested on the penalty for selling oneself by contract—leaning on both sides, mother and son both punished; Teng's application of the law text was not its proper article.
translations.idiomatic: The prosecution began with a charge of unfilial conduct but ended with the penalty for contractual sale of persons—straddling two statutes to condemn both mother and son. Ge Teng's citation simply does not fit the case.

sentences.zh: 嘉所存者大，理在難申，但明教爰發，矜其愚蔽。

translations.literal: What Jia preserved was great; the principle is hard to articulate—but a clear instruction is hereby issued to pity his ignorance and blindness.
translations.idiomatic: Jia's motive was noble though his reasoning was hard to express; the court should recognize his ignorant error and show mercy.

sentences.zh: 夫明德慎罰，文王所以恤下；

translations.literal: Now, manifest virtue and careful punishment—this is how King Wen showed compassion to those below;
translations.idiomatic: Manifest virtue and measured punishment were how King Wen showed compassion to his subjects;

sentences.zh: 議獄緩死，《中孚》所以垂化。

translations.literal: Deliberating on cases and deferring death—this is how the Zhong Fu hexagram handed down transformation.
translations.idiomatic: deliberate review of cases and commutation of death sentences, as the Zhong Fu hexagram teaches, are how sagely rule transforms the people.

sentences.zh: 言情則母為子隱，語敬則禮所不及。

translations.literal: Speaking of sentiment, a mother may conceal a son; speaking of reverence, rites do not extend there.
translations.idiomatic: In matters of feeling, a mother may conceal her son's fault; as for strict ritual propriety, the rites do not extend to such desperate circumstances.

sentences.zh: 今舍乞宥之評，依請殺之條，責敬恭之節，於饑寒之隸，誠非罰疑從輕，寧失有罪之謂也。

translations.literal: Now abandoning the plea for pardon, relying on the article for permission to kill, demanding the standard of reverent respect from a menial in hunger and cold—truly this is not the principle of punishing where doubt exists by leaning toward leniency, and rather letting the guilty go.
translations.idiomatic: To set aside a plea for mercy and apply the statute permitting a parent's request for execution, demanding full ritual propriety from a destitute son and mother, violates the principle of leniency in doubtful cases and the sage maxim that it is better to spare the guilty than execute the innocent.

sentences.zh: 愚以謂降嘉之死，以普春澤之恩；

translations.literal: In my humble view, commutation of Jia's death would spread the grace of spring rain;
translations.idiomatic: I propose that commuting Jia's death would spread the emperor's springtime mercy;

sentences.zh: 赦熊之愆，以明子隱之宜。

translations.literal: Pardoning Xiong's offense would clarify the propriety of a son's concealment.
translations.idiomatic: and pardoning Xiong would affirm the recognized propriety of a mother shielding her son.

sentences.zh: 則蒲亭雖陋，可比德於盛明；

translations.literal: Then though Puting is lowly, one could compare its virtue to an age of splendor;
translations.idiomatic: Though our court may seem humble beside the sage kings, such mercy would compare favorably with the greatest ages of governance;

sentences.zh: 豚魚微物，不獨遺於今化。」

translations.literal: Even pig and fish—tiny creatures—would not alone be left out of present transformation.
translations.idiomatic: and even the lowliest creatures would share in the benevolence of this age."

sentences.zh: 事未判，值赦，並免。

translations.literal: 」The matter had not yet been decided when an amnesty was issued, and all were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Before the court could render judgment, a general amnesty was declared and all parties were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 晦進號衛將軍，轉諮議參軍，領記室。

translations.literal: Hui was promoted to the title of Defender-General, transferred to Consultative Staff Officer, and concurrently headed the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hui was promoted to Defender-General, appointed Consultative Staff Officer, and put in charge of the secretariat staff.

sentences.zh: 元嘉三年，晦將見討，其弟黃門郎皭密信報之，晦問承天曰：「若果爾，卿令我云何？」

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanjia, Hui was about to face punitive action; his younger brother, Yellow Gate Attendant Jiao, sent a secret letter informing him. Hui asked Chengtian: "If it truly comes to that, what would you have me do?
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanjia, Xie Hui learned that punitive action against him was imminent. His younger brother Jiao, a Yellow Gate Attendant, sent a secret warning. Hui asked Chengtian, "If it comes to that, what should I do?

sentences.zh: 承天曰：「以王者之重，舉天下以攻一州，大小既殊，逆順又異，境外求全，上計也。

translations.literal: 」Chengtian said: "With the weight of a king, rallying all under Heaven to attack one province—the scale is already unequal, and the righteous and the rebellious are also different. Seeking self-preservation beyond the borders is the best plan.
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian replied, "A king can mobilize the entire realm against a single province—the odds favor him, and justice favors him as well. Your best course is to flee beyond the frontier and save yourself.

sentences.zh: 其次，以腹心領兵戍於義陽，將軍率眾於夏口一戰，若敗，即趨義陽以出北境，其次也。」

translations.literal: Next, send trusted men to lead troops to garrison at Yiyang; the General himself leads the host to fight one battle at Xiakou—if defeated, then hurry to Yiyang and exit the northern border. This is the second best.
translations.idiomatic: Second best: post your trusted lieutenants with troops at Yiyang while you lead the main force to give battle at Xiakou. If you lose, retreat to Yiyang and escape across the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 晦良久曰：「荊楚用武之國，兵力有餘，且當決戰，走不晚也。」

translations.literal: 」After a long silence Hui said: "Jing and Chu are martial territories; military strength is ample—we should fight a decisive battle first; flight will not be too late."
translations.idiomatic: After a long pause, Hui said, "Jing and Chu are warrior country—we have plenty of troops. We should give decisive battle first; there will still be time to flee if we must."

sentences.zh: 使承天造立表檄。

translations.literal: 」He had Chengtian draft proclamations and call-to-arms documents.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Chengtian to draft the memorials and military proclamations.

sentences.zh: 晦以湘州刺史張邵必不同己，欲遣千人襲之；

translations.literal: Hui believed that Zhang Shao, Regional Inspector of Xiangzhou, would surely not agree with him, and wished to send a thousand men to attack him;
translations.idiomatic: Hui believed that Zhang Shao, the inspector of Xiang province, would not join his cause and planned to send a thousand men to seize him by surprise;

sentences.zh: 承天以為邵意趨未可知，不宜便討。

translations.literal: Chengtian held that Shao's inclinations were not yet known and it was not fitting to attack at once.
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian argued that Zhang Shao's intentions were still unclear and that a preemptive strike was premature.

sentences.zh: 時邵兄茂度為益州，與晦素善，故晦止不遣兵。

translations.literal: At the time Shao's elder brother Maodu was in Yizhou and had long been on good terms with Hui; therefore Hui desisted and did not send troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shao's elder brother Maodu was then in Yi province and had long been friendly with Hui, so Hui abandoned the plan and sent no troops.

sentences.zh: 前益州刺史蕭摹之、前巴西太守劉道產去職還江陵，晦將殺之，承天盡力營救，皆得全免。

translations.literal: The former Regional Inspector of Yizhou Xiao Muzhi and the former Administrator of Baxi Liu Daochan had left office and returned to Jiangling. Hui was about to kill them; Chengtian exerted all effort to rescue them, and all were fully spared.
translations.idiomatic: The former inspector of Yi province, Xiao Muzhi, and the former administrator of Baxi, Liu Daochan, were returning to Jiangling after leaving office. When Hui was about to execute them, Chengtian intervened energetically on their behalf and saved them all.

sentences.zh: 晦既下，承天留府不從。

translations.literal: Once Hui set out downriver, Chengtian remained in the headquarters and did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui marched out against the imperial forces, Chengtian stayed behind at headquarters and refused to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 及到彥之至馬頭，承天自詣歸罪，彥之以其有誠，宥之，使行南蠻府事。

translations.literal: When Dao Yan reached Matou, Chengtian went in person to surrender himself for judgment. Dao Yan, considering his sincerity, pardoned him and had him handle the affairs of the Southern Man headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Dao Yan's army reached Matou, Chengtian went to surrender himself. Dao Yan pardoned him in recognition of his good faith and assigned him to manage the southern barbarian command.

sentences.zh: 七年，彥之北伐，請為右軍錄事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when Dao Yan marched north, Chengtian was requested as Recorder of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, during Dao Yan's northern expedition, Chengtian was appointed recorder on his right-wing staff.

sentences.zh: 及彥之敗退，承天以才非軍旅，得免刑責。

translations.literal: When Dao Yan was defeated and withdrew, Chengtian, because his talents were not suited to military matters, was exempted from criminal punishment.
translations.idiomatic: After Dao Yan's defeat and retreat, Chengtian escaped punishment on the grounds that he was a civilian advisor, not a military commander.

sentences.zh: 以補尚書殿中郎，兼左丞。

translations.literal: He was appointed to fill the post of Gentleman Attendant of the Masters of Writing, concurrently serving as Left Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Gentleman Attendant in the Masters of Writing office, with concurrent duties as left assistant.

sentences.zh: 吳興餘杭民薄道舉為劫。

translations.literal: Bo Daoqü of Yuhang in Wuxing committed robbery.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Daoqü, a commoner of Yuhang in Wuxing commandery, committed robbery.

sentences.zh: 制同籍期親補兵。

translations.literal: The regulation held that consanguine relatives within one registry of the second-degree mourning grade were subject to conscript replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Under the law, consanguine relatives within one household register in the second degree of mourning were liable for military conscription as a penalty.

sentences.zh: 道舉從弟代公、道生等並為大功親，非應在補謫之例，法以代公等母存為期親，則子宜隨母補兵。

translations.literal: Daoqü's younger cousins Daigong, Daosheng, and others were all relatives of the third-degree mourning grade—not within the category for conscript replacement. The law office held that since Daigong and the others' mother was alive as a second-degree relative, the sons ought to follow the mother in conscript replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Daoqü's cousins Daigong, Daosheng, and others were third-degree relatives, not normally subject to the conscription penalty. But the law office argued that because their mother was a second-degree relative still living, her sons should be conscripted along with her.

sentences.zh: 承天議曰：「尋劫制，同籍期親補兵，大功不在此例。

translations.literal: Chengtian argued: "Examining the robbery regulation: consanguine relatives within one registry of the second-degree mourning grade are subject to conscript replacement; third-degree relatives are not within this category.
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian argued: "The robbery statute applies conscription to second-degree relatives within the same household register. Third-degree relatives are not covered.

sentences.zh: 婦人三從，既嫁從夫，夫死從子。

translations.literal: A woman follows three masters: once married she follows her husband; when the husband dies she follows her son.
translations.idiomatic: A woman observes the threefold submission: after marriage she follows her husband; after his death she follows her son.

sentences.zh: 今道舉為劫，若其叔尚存，制應補謫，妻子營居，固其宜也。

translations.literal: Now when Daoqü committed robbery—if his uncle were still alive, the regulation would require conscript replacement, and for wife and sons to share his dwelling—this would indeed be proper.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoqü's case, if his uncle were still alive, conscription of the household would be proper—the wife and children sharing his residence as the law requires.

sentences.zh: 但為劫之時，叔父已沒，代公、道生並是從弟，大功之親，不合補謫。

translations.literal: But at the time of the robbery the uncle was already deceased. Daigong and Daosheng were both younger cousins—third-degree relatives—not fitting the category for conscript replacement.
translations.idiomatic: But at the time of the robbery, the uncle was already dead. Daigong and Daosheng were younger cousins—third-degree relatives—not subject to conscription.

sentences.zh: 今若以叔母為期親，令代公隨母補兵，既違大功不謫之制，又失婦人三從之道。

translations.literal: Now if one treats the uncle's wife as a second-degree relative and orders Daigong to follow his mother in conscript replacement, this both violates the regulation that third-degree relatives are not punished, and also loses the way of a woman's threefold submission.
translations.idiomatic: To treat the aunt as a second-degree relative and conscript Daigong because of his mother violates both the exemption for third-degree kin and the principle of a woman's threefold submission.

sentences.zh: 由於主者守期親之文，不辨男女之異，遠嫌畏負，以生此疑，懼非聖朝恤刑之旨。

translations.literal: Because the responsible official clung to the text on second-degree relatives without distinguishing male from female, fearing distant blame and dreading fault, this doubt arose—I fear it is not the intent of the sage court to show compassion in punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible official clung literally to the statute on second-degree kin without distinguishing the roles of men and women, and out of excessive caution created this confusion. That cannot accord with our court's humane approach to punishment.

sentences.zh: 謂代公等母子並宜見原。」

translations.literal: I hold that Daigong and the others, mother and sons, should all be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: I propose that Daigong, his mother, and his brothers all be pardoned."

sentences.zh: 故司徒掾孔邈奏事未御，邈已喪殯，議者謂不宜仍用邈名，更以見官奏之。

translations.literal: 」The former Senior Clerk of the Minister Over the Masses Kong Miao had submitted a memorial that had not yet been read when Miao had already died and been interred. Deliberators held that it was not proper still to use Miao's name; it should rather be submitted under a currently serving official.
translations.idiomatic: A memorial by the late chief clerk Kong Miao of the Minister Over the Masses had not yet reached the throne when Miao died and was buried. Officials argued that his name should no longer be used and that a living official should resubmit the memorial.

sentences.zh: 承天又議曰：「既沒之名不合奏者，非有它義，正嫌於近不祥耳。

translations.literal: Chengtian argued again: "That a deceased person's name is not submitted—there is no other meaning to this; it is simply scruple over recent inauspiciousness.
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian argued again, "The rule against submitting a dead man's name has no deeper purpose—it merely reflects squeamishness about recent death.

sentences.zh: 奏事一卻，動經歲時，盛明之世，事從簡易，曲嫌細忌，皆應蕩除。」

translations.literal: Once a memorial is returned, it often takes a whole year. In an age of great brilliance, affairs should follow simplicity; crooked scruples and petty taboos should all be swept away."
translations.idiomatic: A returned memorial can languish for a year. In an enlightened age, such mincing taboos should be abolished and procedures simplified."

sentences.zh: 承天為性剛愎，不能屈意朝右，頗以所長侮同列，不為僕射殷景仁所平，出為衡陽內史。

translations.literal: Chengtian was by nature stubborn and willful; he could not bend his will to the great officials at court and often used his own strengths to belittle his colleagues. He was not treated as an equal by the Vice Director Yin Jingren and was sent out as Internal Administrator of Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian was stubborn by nature and refused to defer to senior court officials, often condescending to his colleagues with his expertise. Yin Jingren, the Vice Director, took no liking to him, and Chengtian was posted out as internal administrator of Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 昔在西與士人多不協，在郡又不公清，為州司所糾，被收繫獄，值赦免。

translations.literal: Formerly in the west he had been at odds with many scholars; in the commandery he was again not fair and clean, was impeached by the provincial inspectorate, seized and imprisoned, and was pardoned when an amnesty occurred.
translations.idiomatic: In the west he had long been at odds with many scholars; as administrator he proved corrupt and was impeached by the provincial inspectorate, imprisoned, and then released by amnesty.

sentences.zh: 十六年，除著作佐郎，撰國史。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was appointed Assistant Gentleman Author and compiled the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was appointed assistant historiographer and assigned to compile the dynastic history.

sentences.zh: 承天年已老，而諸佐郎並名家年少，潁川荀伯子嘲之，常呼為奶母。

translations.literal: Chengtian was already old, while all the assistant gentlemen were young men from eminent families. Xun Bozi of Yingchuan mocked him, often calling him "wet nurse."
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian was already elderly, while his fellow assistant historiographers were all young men from eminent families. Xun Bozi of Yingchuan teased him, habitually calling him "the wet nurse."

sentences.zh: 承天曰：「卿當云鳳凰將九子，奶母何言邪！」

translations.literal: Chengtian said: "You ought to say that the phoenix is about to have nine young—what talk is this of a wet nurse!
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian retorted, "You should say the phoenix is about to hatch nine chicks—what nonsense is this about a wet nurse!

sentences.zh: 尋轉太子率更令，著作如故。

translations.literal: 」Shortly thereafter he was transferred to Grand Master of Splendor for the Heir Apparent, retaining his historiographical duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred to Grand Master of Splendor for the Heir Apparent while retaining his historiographical post.

sentences.zh: 時丹陽丁況等久喪不葬，承天議曰：「禮所云還葬，當謂荒儉一時，故許其稱財而不求備。

translations.literal: At the time Ding Kuang of Danyang and others had long left the dead unburied. Chengtian argued: "What the rites call 'return burial' should refer to a time of famine and austerity, hence permitting burial according to one's means without demanding completeness.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Ding Kuang of Danyang and others had left their dead unburied for years. Chengtian argued, "The rites permit 'return burial' only during times of famine and hardship, allowing families to bury according to their means without demanding full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 丁況三家，數年中，葬輒無棺櫬，實由淺情薄恩，同於禽獸者耳。

translations.literal: The three households of Ding Kuang, over several years, whenever they buried had no coffin or outer case—this truly sprang from shallow feeling and thin kindness, the same as beasts.
translations.idiomatic: The three Ding households had buried their dead for years without coffins or outer cases. This reflects not poverty but callous ingratitude little better than beasts.

sentences.zh: 竊以為丁寶等同伍積年，未嘗勸之以義，繩之以法。

translations.literal: I privately hold that Ding Bao and others in the same neighborhood ward, over accumulated years, were never urged with righteousness or bound with law.
translations.idiomatic: For years their neighbors in the same ward never exhorted them with moral duty or restrained them with law.

sentences.zh: 十六年冬，既無新科，又未申明舊制，有何嚴切，欻然相糾。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixteenth year, there was neither a new statute nor a clarification of the old system—what strictness was there, that they should suddenly impeach one another?
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the sixteenth year, no new statute had been issued and no old regulation clarified—what urgency justified sudden denunciation?

sentences.zh: 或由鄰曲分爭，以興此言。

translations.literal: Perhaps it arose from neighborhood quarrels that this talk was stirred up.
translations.idiomatic: The accusations may simply have sprung from neighborhood quarrels.

sentences.zh: 如聞在東諸處，此例既多，江西、淮北尤為不少。

translations.literal: As I have heard, in the eastern regions this case is already numerous; west of the Yangzi and north of the Huai are especially not few.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that such cases are already common in the eastern provinces, especially west of the Yangzi and north of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 若但謫此三人，殆無整肅。

translations.literal: If only these three men are punished, there will scarcely be any real rectification.
translations.idiomatic: Punishing only these three men would scarcely restore order.

sentences.zh: 開其一端，則互相恐動，里伍縣司，競為奸利。

translations.literal: Open one opening, and mutual intimidation will follow; neighborhood wards and county offices will compete in illicit profit.
translations.idiomatic: Open this door and mutual denunciation will spread; neighborhood wards and county offices will compete for illicit gain.

sentences.zh: 財賂既逞，獄訟必繁，懼虧聖明烹鮮之美。

translations.literal: Once bribes have their way, lawsuits will surely multiply—I fear this will impair the sage brilliance of 'cooking small fish' without overhandling.
translations.idiomatic: Once bribery flourishes, lawsuits will multiply, to the detriment of the sage principle of governing lightly, like cooking a small fish without stirring it too much.

sentences.zh: 臣愚謂況等三家，且可勿問，因此附定制旨，若民人葬不如法，同伍當即糾言，三年除服之後，不得追相告列，於事為宜。」

translations.literal: In my foolish view, the three households of Kuang and the others may for the present go unprosecuted. Thereby attach a fixed regulatory purpose: if common people bury contrary to law, the same neighborhood ward should at once report it; after the three-year mourning period has ended, they may not pursue one another with accusations—this would be fitting for affairs."
translations.idiomatic: I propose that the three Ding households be left alone for now, and that a permanent regulation be enacted: when commoners bury improperly, neighbors should report it at once, but after the three-year mourning period no further accusations may be brought. That would serve the public good."

sentences.zh: 十九年，立國子學，以本官領國子博士。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year the Imperial University was established; he retained his original office and concurrently served as Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year the Imperial University was founded, and Chengtian retained his post while serving concurrently as university erudite.

sentences.zh: 皇太子講《孝經》，承天與中庶子顏延之同為執經。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety; Chengtian and the Household Mentor Yan Yanzhi together held the classics.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety, Chengtian and the household mentor Yan Yanzhi served jointly as lecturers.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was transferred to Imperial Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to Imperial Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時索虜侵邊，太祖訪群臣威戎禦遠之略，承天上表曰：

translations.literal: At the time the northern barbarians were invading the borders; the Founder questioned the ministers on strategies for awe-inspiring military display and defense against distant foes. Chengtian submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: When the northern barbarians were raiding the frontier, the Founder asked his ministers for strategies to awe the enemy and secure the borders. Chengtian submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 伏見北藩上事，虜犯青、兗，天慈降鑒，矜此黎元，博逮群策，經綸戎政，臣以愚陋，預聞訪及。

translations.literal: I humbly observe the northern frontier's submitted report: the barbarians are violating Qing and Yan. Heaven's compassion descends in scrutiny, pitying these black-haired people; broadly reaching to all strategies and organizing military administration—I, in my foolish shallowness, have been included in the inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: I have read the northern frontier's report that the barbarians are raiding Qing and Yan provinces. His Majesty, in Heaven's compassion for the people, has sought counsel broadly on military affairs. Though I am unworthy, I have been honored with a request for my views.

sentences.zh: 竊尋獫狁告難，爰自上古，有周之盛，南仲出車，漢氏方隆，衛、霍宣力。

translations.literal: I privately trace how the Xianyun announced calamity from high antiquity onward; in the Zhou at its height, Nan Zhong marched forth with chariots; when the Han house was flourishing, Wei and Huo displayed their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian raids have troubled China since antiquity. At the height of Zhou, Nan Zhong took the field; when the Han flourished, Wei Qing and Huo Qubing won their fame.

sentences.zh: 雖飲馬瀚海，揚旍祁連，事難役繁，天下騷動，委興負海，貲及舟車。

translations.literal: Although horses drank at the Han Sea and banners were raised at Qilian, the affairs were difficult, corvée labor heavy, and all under Heaven stirred; burdens piled like mountains, costs reaching to boats and carts.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Han drove the enemy to drink their horses in the distant sea and raised banners on Qilian Mountain, such campaigns were arduous and costly, stirring the realm and burdening the people to the limit of land and sea transport.

sentences.zh: 凶狡倔強，未肯受弱，得失報復，裁不相補。

translations.literal: Fierce and cunning, stubborn and strong, they would not accept weakness; gains and losses, reprisals and responses, scarcely balanced one another.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy remained fierce and unyielding; gains and losses, attack and reprisal, scarcely balanced each other.

sentences.zh: 宣帝末年，值其乖亂，推亡固存，始獲稽服。

translations.literal: In the last years of Emperor Xuan, when they fell into disorder, he pushed the perishing and strengthened the surviving, and only then obtained their formal submission.
translations.idiomatic: Only in the last years of Emperor Xuan, when the barbarians fell into internal disorder, did the Han exploit their weakness and win formal submission.

sentences.zh: 自晉喪中原，戎狄侵擾，百餘年間，未暇以北虜為念。

translations.literal: Since Jin lost the central plains, the Rong and Di harassed and raided; for more than a hundred years there was no leisure to think of the northern barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jin lost the central plains, barbarian raids continued for more than a century, and the court had no leisure to concern itself with the northern enemy.

sentences.zh: 大宋啟祚，兩耀靈武，而懷德畏威，用自款納。

translations.literal: When Great Song began its reign, both sun and moon displayed spiritual martial prowess, yet the barbarians cherished virtue and feared awe, and thereby of themselves came to offer submission.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song dynasty arose, its military glory shone forth, and the barbarians, awed by its virtue and power, voluntarily submitted.

sentences.zh: 陛下臨御以來，羈縻遵養，十餘年中，貢譯不絕。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty's accession, they have been bridled and nurtured in compliance; for more than ten years tribute and interpreters have not ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty's accession, the court has restrained and nurtured them, and for more than ten years tribute missions have never ceased.

sentences.zh: 去歲三王出鎮，思振遠圖，獸心易駭，遂生猜懼，背違信約，深構攜隙。

translations.literal: Last year the three princes went out to their posts; thinking to revive distant designs, the beast-heart is easily startled, and so suspicion and fear arose—they violated faith and treaty and deeply constructed estrangement.
translations.idiomatic: Last year, when the three princes took up their frontier posts with plans to recover lost territory, the barbarians' suspicious nature was easily alarmed. They broke faith, and deep enmity arose between us.

sentences.zh: 貪禍恣毒，無因自反，恐烽燧之警，必自此始。

translations.literal: Greedy for calamity and unrestrained in poison, they have no cause to turn back of themselves—I fear that beacon-fires of alarm will surely begin from this.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy and ruthless, they will not turn back of their own accord. I fear that frontier alarms will begin from this moment.

sentences.zh: 臣素庸懦，才不經武，率其管窺，謹撰《安邊論》。

translations.literal: I have always been mediocre and timid; my talent does not pass through military affairs. Leading my narrow-glimpse view, I respectfully composed the "Treatise on Securing the Borders."
translations.idiomatic: I am by nature mediocre and timid, with no military expertise. Drawing on my limited understanding, I have respectfully drafted a "Treatise on Securing the Borders."

sentences.zh: 意及淺末，懼無可采。

translations.literal: The ideas reach only shallow ends; I fear there is nothing worth adopting.
translations.idiomatic: My views are shallow and I fear they merit no attention.

sentences.zh: 若得詢之朝列，辨核同異，庶或開引群慮，研盡眾謀，短長畢陳，當否可見。

translations.literal: If it may be inquired of the court ranks, distinguishing and verifying sameness and difference, perhaps it will open and draw forth the collective deliberations, exhaustively study the multitude of plans, with strengths and weaknesses all set forth and what is fitting or not made visible.
translations.idiomatic: If the court will discuss it among the ministers, weighing agreement and disagreement, it may draw out broader counsel and exhaust the range of proposals, so that strengths and weaknesses are fully aired and the right course becomes clear.

sentences.zh: 其論曰：

translations.literal: The treatise says:
translations.idiomatic: The treatise reads:

sentences.zh: 漢世言備匈奴之策，不過二科，武夫盡征伐之謀，儒生講和親之約，課其所言，互有遠志。

translations.literal: In Han times, speaking of strategies to guard against the Xiongnu, there were no more than two categories: military men exhausted plans of conquest, Confucian scholars discoursed on treaties of marriage alliance. Examining what they said, each had distant aims.
translations.idiomatic: Han discussions of how to guard against the Xiongnu fell into two schools: warriors urged all-out conquest, scholars advocated marriage alliances. Each camp pursued its own distant aim.

sentences.zh: 加塞漠之外，胡敵掣肘，必未能摧鋒引日，規自開張。

translations.literal: Moreover, beyond the frontier deserts the Hu enemy is checked and constrained; they surely cannot break our edge and prolong the day, planning to open and expand on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, beyond the desert frontier the barbarians are constrained and cannot sustain a prolonged offensive or expand their territory at will.

sentences.zh: 當由往年冀土之民，附化者眾，二州臨境，三王出藩，經略既張，宏圖將舉，士女延望，華、夷慕義。

translations.literal: This should be because in former years the people of Ji territory, many submitted to transformation; the two provinces border the frontier; the three princes went out to their fiefs; grand strategy was already spread, the great design about to be raised—scholars and women stretched in hope, Chinese and barbarians admired righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The cause lies rather in recent years: many people of Ji province have submitted to our rule; the two frontier provinces border the enemy; the three princes have taken up their posts; our grand strategy is unfolding and the people, Chinese and barbarian alike, look to us with hope.

sentences.zh: 故昧於小利，且自矜侈，外示餘力，內堅偽眾。

translations.literal: Therefore blind to small profit and for the moment self-aggrandizing, outwardly displaying surplus strength, inwardly stiffening a false multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Blinded by petty advantage, they have grown arrogant, making a show of strength while secretly hardening their forces.

sentences.zh: 今若務存遵養，許其自新，雖未可羈致北闕，猶足鎮靜邊境。

translations.literal: Now if we devote ourselves to preserving nurture and compliance, permitting them to renew themselves, although we may not yet be able to tether them to the northern gate-tower, it is still enough to calm and quiet the borders.
translations.idiomatic: If we continue to restrain and nurture them and permit repentance, we may not yet bring them to court, but we can still secure the frontier.

sentences.zh: 然和親事重，當盡廟算，誠非愚短，所能究言。

translations.literal: Yet the matter of marriage alliance is weighty and should exhaust temple calculations—truly this is not what my foolish shallowness can fully articulate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet peace through alliance is a weighty matter requiring full deliberation in the ancestral temple—beyond what my limited understanding can fully address.

sentences.zh: 若追蹤衛、霍瀚海之志，時事不等，致功亦殊。

translations.literal: If we pursue the Han Sea ambition of Wei and Huo, the times are not equal and the achievement of merit is also different.
translations.idiomatic: To emulate Wei Qing and Huo Qubing's ambition to drive the enemy to the distant sea would be to ignore how times differ and how outcomes differ as well.

sentences.zh: 寇雖習戰未久，又全據燕、趙，跨帶秦、魏，山河之險，終古如一。

translations.literal: Although the enemy has not long been practiced in warfare, they fully hold Yan and Zhao, spanning and girdling Qin and Wei—the peril of mountains and rivers is from antiquity to the present a single constant.
translations.idiomatic: Though the enemy has not long been at war, they hold all of Yan and Zhao and control the territories linking Qin and Wei. The natural defenses of mountains and rivers have been the same since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 自非大田淮、泗，內實青、徐，使民有贏儲，野有積穀，然後分命方、召，總率虎旅，精卒十萬，使一舉蕩夷，則不足稍勤王師，以勞天下。

translations.literal: Unless we first make great fields of Huai and Si, fill inwardly Qing and Xu, cause the people to have surplus stores and the wilds to have accumulated grain—only then appointing Fang and Shao, commanding tiger hosts, elite soldiers in the tens of thousands, to make one sweep and level the barbarians—it is not enough slightly to mobilize the royal army and weary all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Unless we first develop the Huai and Si regions, strengthen Qing and Xu within, ensure that the people have surplus grain and the countryside ample stores, and only then dispatch commanders like the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao at the head of a hundred thousand elite troops to sweep the barbarians away—it is not enough merely to mobilize the imperial army and weary the realm.

sentences.zh: 何以言之？

translations.literal: Why do I say this?
translations.idiomatic: Why do I say this?

sentences.zh: 今遺黎習亂，志在偷安，非皆恥為左衽，遠慕冠冕，徒以殘害剝辱，視息無寄，故繦負歸國，先後相尋。

translations.literal: Now the remnant people are accustomed to disorder; their will is set on stealing peace—they are not all ashamed to wear the left lapel and admire court caps from afar; they are merely because of mutilation, harm, stripping, and insult, with breath viewed and no refuge, that they come swaddled on the back to return to the state, one after another in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the lost north are accustomed to turmoil and care only for survival. They are not all ashamed to wear barbarian dress or yearning for Chinese civilization; they come to us swaddled on their backs because oppression and plunder have left them nowhere else to turn.

sentences.zh: 虜既不能校勝循理，攻城掠地，而輕兵掩襲，急在驅殘，是其所以速怨召禍，滅亡之日。

translations.literal: The barbarians, being unable to compare victory and follow principle, storm cities and seize land, yet with light troops make surprise raids, urgent in driving off and slaughtering the remnant—this is why they quickly summon resentment and invite calamity; the day of their destruction.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians cannot win by fair contest or seize territory by siege; they rely on swift raids to slaughter and drive out the people. That is why they quickly earn hatred and invite their own destruction.

sentences.zh: 今若遣軍追討，報其侵暴，大翦幽、冀，屠城破邑，則聖朝愛育黎元，方濟之以道。

translations.literal: Now if we send armies in pursuit to retaliate for their invasion and violence, greatly cutting down You and Ji, slaughtering cities and breaking towns—then the sage court's cherishing nurture of the black-haired people is just about to succor them with the Way.
translations.idiomatic: If we now send armies in pursuit, retaliating for their raids by ravaging You and Ji, slaughtering in cities and towns, we would contradict the sage court's mission to cherish and succor the people.

sentences.zh: 若但欲撫其歸附，伐罪弔民，則駿馬奔走，不肯來征，徒興巨費，無損於彼。

translations.literal: If we only wish to soothe their coming submission, punishing guilt and comforting the people, then fine horses will run at full speed and refuse to come to campaign—merely raising vast expense with no harm to them.
translations.idiomatic: If we wish only to welcome those who submit and wage a punitive campaign to succor the people, the enemy's swift cavalry will refuse pitched battle, and we will incur vast expense to no effect.

sentences.zh: 復奇兵深入，殺敵破軍，苟陵患未盡，則困獸思鬥，報復之役，將遂無已。

translations.literal: Again, if elite troops penetrate deeply, kill the enemy and break their armies—if grievance and insult are not exhausted, then cornered beasts will think to fight; campaigns of reprisal will then have no end.
translations.idiomatic: If we send elite troops deep into enemy territory to kill and rout their armies, any remaining grievance will make them fight like cornered beasts, and cycles of reprisal will never end.

sentences.zh: 斯秦、漢之末策，輪臺之所悔也。

translations.literal: This is the late policy of Qin and Han, what the Luntai edict regretted.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the failed late policy of Qin and Han, the very course that the Luntai edict repented.

sentences.zh: 安邊固守，於計為長。

translations.literal: Securing the borders through firm defense is, in planning, the long course.
translations.idiomatic: Securing the borders through firm defense is the soundest long-term strategy.

sentences.zh: 臣以安邊之計，備在史策，李牧言其端，嚴尤申其要，大略舉矣。

translations.literal: I hold that the plan for securing borders is fully recorded in historical annals: Li Mu stated its beginning, Yan You expounded its essentials—the great outline has already been set forth.
translations.idiomatic: The strategy for securing the borders is fully recorded in history: Li Mu stated its principles, Yan You elaborated its essentials—the broad outline is already clear.

sentences.zh: 曹、孫之霸，才均智敵，江、淮之間，不居各數百里。

translations.literal: In the hegemony of Cao and Sun, talents were equal and wisdoms matched foes; between the Yangzi and Huai they did not dwell more than several hundred li apart.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao and Sun Quan contended for supremacy, their talents and strategies were evenly matched, and their domains along the Yangzi and Huai lay only a few hundred li apart.

sentences.zh: 魏舍合肥，退保新城，江陵移民南涘，濡須之戍，家停羨溪。

translations.literal: Wei abandoned Hefei and withdrew to guard Xincheng; Jiangling moved its people to the southern shore; the garrison at Ruxu halted its households at Xian Creek.
translations.idiomatic: Wei abandoned Hefei and withdrew to Xincheng; Jiangling moved its population south of the river; the garrison at Ruxu quartered families along Xian Creek.

sentences.zh: 及表陵之屯，民夷散雜，晉宣王以為宜從江南以北岸，曹爽不許，果亡柤中，此皆前代之殷鑒也。

translations.literal: When it came to the encampment at Biaoling, with Chinese and barbarians scattered and mixed, Jin's Xuan Emperor held that one ought to move from south of the Yangzi to the north bank; Cao Shuang did not permit it, and they indeed perished in Zuzhong—these are all stern mirrors of former ages.
translations.idiomatic: At the Biaoling encampment, with Chinese and barbarians intermixed, Sima Yi urged moving populations from south of the Yangzi to the north bank; Cao Shuang refused, and defeat at Zuzhong followed. These are all stern lessons from history.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 斥候之郊，非畜牧之地，非耕桑之邑。

translations.literal: The outskirts where scouts are posted are not lands for pasturing livestock, not settlements for plowing and mulberry.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier zones where scouts operate are neither pastureland nor farmland.

sentences.zh: 故堅壁清野，以俟其來，整甲繕兵，以乘其敝。

translations.literal: Therefore fortify walls and clear the countryside to await their coming; put armor in order and repair weapons to seize their exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore fortify defenses and clear the countryside to await their coming; ready armor and weapons to strike when they are spent.

sentences.zh: 雖時有古今，勢有強弱，保民全境，不出此塗。

translations.literal: Although times have antiquity and present, and circumstances have strength and weakness, to preserve the people and secure the whole territory does not depart from this path.
translations.idiomatic: Though times and relative strength differ, the way to preserve the people and secure the whole territory does not change.

sentences.zh: 要而歸之有四：一曰移遠就近；

translations.literal: In essentials, returning to it there are four points: first, move the distant near;
translations.idiomatic: In sum, the strategy has four elements: first, relocate distant populations closer to safety;

sentences.zh: 二曰浚復城隍；

translations.literal: second, dredge and restore moats and walls;
translations.idiomatic: second, dredge moats and repair city walls;

sentences.zh: 三曰纂偶車牛；

translations.literal: third, assemble and pair carts and oxen;
translations.idiomatic: third, organize carts and draft animals;

sentences.zh: 四曰計丁課仗。

translations.literal: fourth, calculate households and levy weapons.
translations.idiomatic: fourth, register households and levy arms.

sentences.zh: 良守疆其土田，驍帥振其風略。

translations.literal: Good administrators border and guard their fields; fierce generals stir their wind and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Capable administrators should secure the farmland; valiant commanders should inspire martial spirit.

sentences.zh: 搜獵宣其號令，俎豆訓其廉恥。

translations.literal: Hunting drills proclaim their orders; ritual vessels instruct their sense of shame.
translations.idiomatic: Hunting exercises should enforce discipline; ritual instruction should cultivate honor and shame.

sentences.zh: 縣爵以縻之，設禁以威之。

translations.literal: Suspend ranks to tether them; establish prohibitions to awe them.
translations.idiomatic: Bestow ranks to bind them to service; impose prohibitions to enforce discipline.

sentences.zh: 徭稅有程，寬猛相濟。

translations.literal: Corvée and tax have their schedules; lenience and severity assist each other.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée and taxation should follow fixed schedules, with lenience and severity balanced.

sentences.zh: 比及十載，民知義方。

translations.literal: By the time of ten years, the people will know the way of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten years the people will understand their moral duty.

sentences.zh: 然後簡將授奇，揚旌雲朔，風卷河冀，電掃嵩恆，燕弧折卻，代馬摧足，秦首斬其右臂，吳蹄絕其左肩，銘功於燕然之阿，饗徒於金微之曲。

translations.literal: Only then select generals and confer stratagems, raise banners in Yun and Shuo, wind rolling through He and Ji, lightning sweeping Song and Heng—Yan's bows bent back, Dai's horses with crushed hooves, Qin's head severing its right arm, Wu's hooves cutting off its left shoulder—inscribe merit on the slope of Yanshan, feast the troops in the bend of Jinwei.
translations.idiomatic: Only then may we select commanders and deploy brilliant stratagems, raise banners in the northern frontier, sweep like wind through Hebei and Ji, strike like lightning across the sacred mountains—break the enemy's bowmen of Yan, shatter the cavalry of Dai, sever their right arm in Qin and cut their left shoulder in Wu—inscribe our merit on Mount Yanshan and feast the troops at Jinwei.

sentences.zh: 寇雖亂亡有徵，昧弱易取，若天時人事，或未盡符，抑銳俟機，宜審其算。

translations.literal: Although the enemy, though disorder and ruin have their signs, being dim and weak is easy to take—if heavenly timing and human affairs perhaps do not fully accord, restrain sharpness and await the opportunity; one should carefully examine the reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Though the enemy shows signs of disorder and weakness, if heaven and human affairs are not yet fully aligned, we should restrain our ardor, await the right moment, and calculate carefully.

sentences.zh: 若邊戍未增，星居布野，勤惰異教，貧富殊資，疆場之民，多懷彼此，虜在去就，不根本業，難可驅率，易在振盪。

translations.literal: If border garrisons are not increased, scattered dwellings spread across the wilds, diligence and sloth follow different teachings, poor and rich have separate resources—the people of the marches mostly harbor mutual doubts; the barbarians in staying or leaving do not root themselves in their occupations—hard to drive and lead, easy to be shaken and disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: If border garrisons are not strengthened while scattered settlements dot the countryside, if diligence and indolence follow different customs and rich and poor hold unequal means, then frontier people will harbor divided loyalties. The barbarians, unsettled in their allegiance and without rooted livelihoods, cannot be reliably led and are easily thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 又狡虜之性，食肉衣皮，以馳騁為儀容，以游獵為南畝，非有車輿之安，宮室之衛。

translations.literal: Moreover, the crafty barbarians by nature eat meat and wear hides, take galloping as their bearing and hunting as their south-field, without the ease of carriage and chariot or the guard of halls and chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the barbarians are by nature meat-eaters who clothe themselves in hides; they take horsemanship as their dignity and hunting as their livelihood, knowing nothing of the comforts of carriages or the protection of walled dwellings.

sentences.zh: 櫛風沐雨，不以為勞；

translations.literal: Combing the wind and bathing in rain—they do not regard it as toil;
translations.idiomatic: They endure wind and rain without counting it hardship;

sentences.zh: 露宿草寢，維其常性；

translations.literal: sleeping in the dew and bedding on grass—this alone is their constant nature;
translations.idiomatic: sleeping under the open sky on grass is their ordinary way.

sentences.zh: 勝則競利，敗不羞走，彼來或驟，而此已奔疲。

translations.literal: When victorious they compete for profit; when defeated they are not ashamed to flee. Those come sometimes in sudden raids, while we are already spent from running in exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: When they win they rush for spoils; when they lose they flee without shame. They may arrive in a sudden rush while our men are already worn out from pursuit.

sentences.zh: 且今春逾濟，既獲其利，乘勝忸忲，未虞天誅，比及秋末，容更送死。

translations.literal: Moreover, this spring they crossed the Ji, already obtaining their profit; riding victory they are brazen and arrogant, not anticipating heaven's punishment—by autumn's end perhaps they will come again to deliver themselves to death.
translations.idiomatic: This spring they crossed the Ji and took their fill of plunder; flushed with victory they grow reckless, heedless of retribution—and by autumn's end they may well return to throw themselves against us again.

sentences.zh: 猋騎蟻聚，輕兵鳥集，並踐禾稼，焚爇閭井，雖邊將多略，未審何以禦之。

translations.literal: Whirlwind cavalry gather like ants; light troops cluster like birds. Together they trample the grain crops and burn villages and wells. Though border generals have many stratagems, it is not clear by what means to repel them.
translations.idiomatic: Their swift horsemen swarm like ants and their light troops gather like flocking birds, trampling the harvest and burning homesteads. Though our frontier commanders are resourceful, it is hard to see how they can be held off.

sentences.zh: 若盛師連屯，廢農必眾，馳車奔馹，起役必遲，散金行賞，損費必大，換土客戍，怨曠必繁。

translations.literal: If one deploys massive armies in linked encampments, those abandoning agriculture will surely be many; if chariots and couriers race on relays, mobilization will surely be slow; if gold is scattered for rewards, losses will surely be great; if troops from other regions are exchanged for garrison duty, resentment and desertion will surely multiply.
translations.idiomatic: Massing armies in chained encampments would idle countless farmers; racing couriers and chariots would make mobilization slow; scattering gold for rewards would drain the treasury; rotating garrisons of outsiders would breed resentment and desertion.

sentences.zh: 孰若因民所居，並脩農戰，無動眾之勞，有捍衛之實，其為利害，優劣相縣也。

translations.literal: How does that compare to following where the people dwell, jointly cultivating agriculture and warfare, without the toil of mobilizing the masses yet with the substance of defense—their benefit and harm, superior and inferior, are separated by a wide margin.
translations.idiomatic: Far better to work from where the people already live, training them in both farming and fighting—no need to mobilize the masses, yet real defense is gained. The difference in cost and benefit is immense.

sentences.zh: 一曰移遠就近，以實內地。

translations.literal: First: move those from afar to nearer places, to fill the inner lands.
translations.idiomatic: First: relocate distant populations closer in, to strengthen the interior.

sentences.zh: 今青、兗舊民，冀州新附，在界首者二萬家，此寇之資也。

translations.literal: Now the old inhabitants of Qing and Yan, the newly attached of Ji Province—at the border marches are twenty thousand households; this is provision for the raiders.
translations.idiomatic: The old settlers of Qing and Yan and the newly submitted people of Ji number twenty thousand households on the frontier—resources for the enemy.

sentences.zh: 今悉可內徙，青州民移東萊、平昌、北海諸郡，泰山以南，南至下邳，左沭右沂，田良野沃，西阻蘭陵，北扼大峴，四塞之內，其號險固。

translations.literal: Now all can be moved inward. Qing Province people should shift to Donglai, Pingchang, Beihai and other commanderies—from south of Mount Tai, south to Xiapi, Shu on the left and Yi on the right, fields excellent and wilderness fertile, blocked on the west by Lanling, held on the north by Great Xian, within four passes—its name is secure and strong.
translations.idiomatic: All may now be resettled inland. The people of Qingzhou should move to Donglai, Pingchang, Beihai, and related commanderies—the region south of Mount Tai down to Xiapi, bounded by the Shu and Yi rivers, with rich fields and fertile countryside, Lanling blocking the west and Great Xian guarding the north, enclosed within four passes—a terrain famed for its strength.

sentences.zh: 民性重遷，闇於圖始，無虜之時，喜生咨怨。

translations.literal: The people's nature weighs against moving; they are blind to beginnings. When there are no barbarians, they happily give rise to complaints and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: People naturally resist relocation and cannot see long-term advantage; in peacetime they readily complain.

sentences.zh: 今新被鈔掠，餘懼未息，若曉示安危，居以樂土，宜其歌抃就路，視遷如歸。

translations.literal: Now newly having suffered plunder and raid, remaining fear not yet subsided—if one clarifies safety and danger and settles them on fertile land, it is fitting they should clap and sing on the road, viewing relocation as returning home.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh from looting and raid, their fear not yet faded, if we show them security and settle them on good land, they should go forth clapping and singing, treating the move as coming home.

sentences.zh: 二曰浚復城隍，以增阻防。

translations.literal: Second: dredge and restore city walls and moats, to increase obstructive defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Second: repair city walls and moats to strengthen defensive barriers.

sentences.zh: 舊秋冬收斂，民人入保，所以警備暴客，使防衛有素也。

translations.literal: Formerly in autumn and winter after harvest, the people entered protected settlements—this was to warn against and prepare for violent intruders, so that defense had routine.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly after the autumn harvest people would withdraw into fortified settlements, a standing guard against raiders so defense was systematic.

sentences.zh: 古之城池，處處皆有，今雖頹毀，猶可修治。

translations.literal: The cities and moats of antiquity existed everywhere; though today they are ruined and collapsed, they can still be repaired.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient walls and moats stood everywhere; though ruined now, they can still be restored.

sentences.zh: 粗計戶數，量其所容，新徙之家，悉著城內，假其經用，為之閭伍，納稼築場，還在一處。

translations.literal: Roughly calculating households and measuring capacity, newly relocated families should all be registered within cities; lend them their resources, make for them neighborhood and five-household groups, bring in harvest and build threshing floors—returning everything to one place.
translations.idiomatic: Estimate household numbers and capacity, register all new settlers within the walls, supply their needs, organize them into wards and groups, and concentrate harvest and threshing in one place.

sentences.zh: 婦子守家，長吏為師，丁夫匹婦，春夏佃牧。

translations.literal: Wives and children guard the home; elders and officials serve as instructors. Able men and matched women—in spring and summer farm and herd.
translations.idiomatic: Women and children remain at home while officials act as instructors; men and their wives farm and pasture in spring and summer.

sentences.zh: 寇至之時，一城千室，堪戰之士，不下二千，其餘羸弱，猶能登陴鼓噪。

translations.literal: When raiders come, a city of a thousand households has no fewer than two thousand able warriors; the rest, though weak, can still mount the parapets and beat the drums shouting.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy comes, a city of a thousand households can field at least two thousand fighting men; even the weak can man the walls and raise the alarm.

sentences.zh: 十則圍之，兵家舊說，戰士二千，足抗群虜三萬矣。

translations.literal: When tenfold one besieges—the old military saying. Two thousand warriors suffice to resist thirty thousand barbarian hosts.
translations.idiomatic: The classic military maxim says ten besiege one; two thousand defenders can hold off thirty thousand barbarians.

sentences.zh: 三曰纂偶車牛，以飾戎械。

translations.literal: Third: assemble paired oxen and carts to equip military implements.
translations.idiomatic: Third: organize teams of oxen and carts as military equipment.

sentences.zh: 計千家之資，不下五百耦牛，為車五百兩。

translations.literal: Calculating the resources of a thousand households, there are no fewer than five hundred yoked teams of oxen, making five hundred chariot-carts.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand households can muster at least five hundred ox-teams—five hundred carts.

sentences.zh: 參合鉤連，以衛其眾。

translations.literal: Join and link them with hooks to guard their masses.
translations.idiomatic: Link them together with couplings to shield the community.

sentences.zh: 設使城不可固，平行趨險，賊所不能干。

translations.literal: Suppose the city cannot be held firm—moving on level ground toward danger, the bandits cannot interfere.
translations.idiomatic: If walls cannot hold, they can move along level paths to safer ground where raiders cannot reach them.

sentences.zh: 既已族居，易可檢括。

translations.literal: Since they already dwell in clan settlements, they are easy to muster and control.
translations.idiomatic: Clustered together, they are easy to register and mobilize.

sentences.zh: 號令先明，民知夙戒。

translations.literal: Orders and commands announced beforehand—the people know early warning.
translations.idiomatic: Clear advance orders ensure the people are forewarned.

sentences.zh: 有急徵發，信宿可聚。

translations.literal: When there is urgency for levy and dispatch, within one or two nights they can gather.
translations.idiomatic: In an emergency they can be assembled within a day or two.

sentences.zh: 四曰計丁課仗，勿使有闕。

translations.literal: Fourth: calculate adult males and assign weapons, do not let there be gaps.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: register every able man and assign arms, leaving none unarmed.

sentences.zh: 千家之邑，戰士二千，隨其便能，各自有仗，素所服習，銘刻由己，還保輸之於庫，出行請以自衛。

translations.literal: A settlement of a thousand households has two thousand warriors; according to their capacities each has weapons they are accustomed to and practiced in, engraved by themselves; when returning to guard they deposit them in the arsenal, and when going out they request them for self-defense.
