translations.idiomatic: A settlement of a thousand households fields two thousand fighters, each equipped according to skill with familiar, personally marked weapons stored in the armory and issued for outings.

sentences.zh: 弓干利鐵，民不辦得者，官以漸充之，數年之內，軍用粗備矣。

translations.literal: Bows, shafts, and sharp iron that the people cannot obtain on their own—the government gradually supplies them; within several years, military use will be roughly complete.
translations.idiomatic: Where civilians cannot afford bows and blades, the state should gradually supply them; within a few years armaments will be largely ready.

sentences.zh: 臣聞軍國異容，施於封畿之內；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that army and state differ in form; applied within the royal domain's interior—
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that military and civil administration differ in form within the capital domains;

sentences.zh: 兵農並修，在於疆場之表。

translations.literal: soldiery and agriculture jointly cultivated belong at the marches' outer edge.
translations.idiomatic: while combined farming and fighting belongs on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 攻守之宜，皆因其習，任其怯勇。

translations.literal: What suits attack and defense—all follow their customs, allow their timidity and courage.
translations.idiomatic: Tactics for attack and defense should follow local custom and suit each man's courage or timidity.

sentences.zh: 山陵川陸之形，寒暑溫涼之氣，各由本性，易則害生。

translations.literal: The forms of mountains, hills, rivers, and plains; the qi of cold, heat, warmth, and cool—each follows its native nature; change brings harm to life.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain, hill, river, and plain each have their nature; cold, heat, and climate follow local habit—change breeds harm.

sentences.zh: 是故戍申作師，遠屯清濟，功費既重，嗟怨亦深。

translations.literal: Therefore in the gengshen year troops were raised, encamped far at Qing and Ji—the achievement's cost already heavy, sighing and resentment also deep.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the gengshen campaign that garrisoned far along the Qing and Ji cost heavily in effort and bred deep resentment.

sentences.zh: 以臣料之，未若即用彼眾之易也。

translations.literal: By your servant's reckoning, it is not as good as directly using those masses—easier.
translations.idiomatic: In my judgment, using the local population directly would be far easier.

sentences.zh: 管子治齊，寄令在民；

translations.literal: Guanzi governed Qi by lodging orders in the people;
translations.idiomatic: Guan Zhong governed Qi by entrusting authority to the people;

sentences.zh: 商君為秦，設以耕戰。

translations.literal: Lord Shang made Qin, establishing farming and warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Shang of Qin instituted the system of farming and fighting.

sentences.zh: 終申威定霸，行其志業，非苟任強，實由有數。

translations.literal: Qin finally extended its prestige and fixed its hegemony, carrying out its ambition and enterprise—not rashly relying on strength alone, but truly because it had method.
translations.idiomatic: Qin at last achieved supremacy and realized its ambitions—not by crude force alone but by systematic method.

sentences.zh: 梁用走卒，其邦自滅；

translations.literal: Liang used running foot-soldiers, its state perished of itself;
translations.idiomatic: Liang employed hired runners and perished;

sentences.zh: 齊用技擊，厥眾亦離。

translations.literal: Qi used striking-and-kicking fighters, its masses also dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Qi relied on martial champions and its forces scattered as well.

sentences.zh: 漢、魏以來，茲制漸絕，搜田非復先王之禮，治兵徒逞耳目之欲，有急之日，民不知戰，至乃廣延賞募，奉以厚秩，發遽奔救，天下騷然。

translations.literal: From Han and Wei onward this system gradually ceased; hunting-field exercises are no longer the former kings' ritual; training troops merely indulges eye and ear pleasure. On days of urgency the people do not know warfare—ultimately broadening rewards and recruitment, bestowing generous salaries, dispatching urgent runners for rescue, and all under Heaven in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han and Wei this system has faded; military hunts no longer follow ancient ritual, and drill serves only display. When crisis comes the people do not know how to fight, and the court must offer lavish bounties, send urgent rescuers, throwing the realm into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 方伯刺史，拱手坐聽，自無經略，唯望朝廷遣軍，此皆忘戰之害，不教之失也。

translations.literal: Regional inspectors and governors sit with folded hands listening, themselves without strategy, only hoping the court sends armies—this is all the harm of forgetting warfare, the fault of not teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Regional governors sit idle without strategy, merely awaiting imperial armies—all the harm of forgetting war and failing to train.

sentences.zh: 今移民實內，浚治城隍，族居聚處，課其騎射，長吏簡試，差品能不，甲科上第，漸就優別，明其勳才，表言州郡。

translations.literal: Now relocate people to fill the interior, dredge and repair walls and moats, clan-dwell and gather together, assign their riding and archery; chief officials select and test, grade capacity and ability—Grade A top rank gradually receives preferential distinction; clarify their merit and talent; memorialize to provinces and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Resettle populations inland, repair walls, cluster communities, drill them in archery and riding; officials should test and grade them, promoting top performers and reporting merit to the provinces.

sentences.zh: 如此則屯部有常，不遷其業。

translations.literal: Thus garrison units have constancy, their occupations not shifted.
translations.idiomatic: Thus garrison districts remain stable and occupations unchanged.

sentences.zh: 內護老弱，外通官塗，朋曹素定，同憂等樂，情由習親，藝因事著，晝戰見貌足相識，夜戰聞聲足相救，斯教戰之一隅，先哲之遺術。

translations.literal: Within they protect the old and weak; outward they connect to official paths. Peer groups long settled share worry and joy equally. Sentiment comes through familiar intimacy; skill shows through affairs. Day battle—seeing faces suffices to know one another; night battle—hearing voices suffices to rescue one another. This is one corner of teaching warfare—the leftover arts of the ancient sages.
translations.idiomatic: They protect the weak within and maintain contact with officials without; settled companions share sorrows and joys; familiarity breeds trust and practice breeds skill. By day fighters recognize one another's faces; by night they know one another's voices—a fragment of the ancients' way of training for war.

sentences.zh: 論者必以古城荒毀，難可修復。

translations.literal: Discussers surely take ancient cities as desolate and ruined, hard to restore.
translations.idiomatic: Critics will surely object that ruined ancient cities cannot be restored.

sentences.zh: 今不謂頓便加功，整麗如舊，但欲先定民，營其閭術，墉壑存者，因而即之，其有毀缺，權時柵斷。

translations.literal: Now I do not mean immediately to add labor and make them splendid as of old—only to first settle the people, lay out their neighborhood lanes; where ramparts and moats survive, build upon them; where there are ruins and gaps, provisionally set palisades.
translations.idiomatic: I do not propose instantly restoring them to former splendor, but first settling the people and organizing wards—using surviving walls where possible and erecting temporary palisades where broken.

sentences.zh: 足以禦彼輕兵，防遏遊騎，假以方將，漸就只立。

translations.literal: This suffices to repel their light troops and check roaming cavalry; loaned to the proper generals, gradually it can be brought to completion.
translations.idiomatic: Enough to hold off light raiders and roaming horsemen; given time and proper commanders, full restoration can follow.

sentences.zh: 車牛之賦，課仗之宜，攻守所資，軍國之要，今因民所利，導而率之。

translations.literal: The levy of carts and oxen, the suitability of assigning weapons—what attack and defense rely on, the state's military essentials—now follow what benefits the people and lead them onward.
translations.idiomatic: Ox-carts and weapon levies, essentials of defense and statecraft, should follow what benefits the people and guide them accordingly.

sentences.zh: 耕農之器，為府庫之寶，田蠶之氓，兼城之用，千家總倍旅之兵，萬戶具全軍之眾，兵強而敵不戒，國富而民不勞，比於優復隊伍，坐食廩糧者，不可同年而校矣。

translations.literal: Farming tools become the treasury's treasure; field and silkworm commoners double as city users. A thousand households total double a brigade's troops; ten thousand households possess a full army's masses. Troops strong yet the enemy unwarned; state rich yet the people unlabored—compared with favored exemption groups who sit and eat granary grain, they cannot be weighed in the same year.
translations.idiomatic: Farming tools become armory treasure; farmers double as defenders. A thousand households equal twice a brigade; ten thousand households a full army—strong forces the enemy does not expect, a rich state without exhausting the people. Nothing compares to privileged units that sit idle on government grain.

sentences.zh: 今承平未久，邊令弛縱，弓竿利鐵，既不都斷，往歲棄甲，垂二十年，課其所住，理應消壞。

translations.literal: Now long peace has not lasted; border laws are lax. Bows, shafts, and sharp iron are neither fully prohibited. Armour abandoned in past years—nearly twenty years—tracking where they dwell, reason says they should be destroyed and ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Peace has not lasted long and frontier laws are lax; weapons are not fully controlled, and armour abandoned for nearly twenty years must by now have decayed.

sentences.zh: 謂宜申明舊科，嚴加禁塞，諸商賈往來，幢隊挾藏者，皆以軍法治之。

translations.literal: Your servant says the old statutes should be clarified, prohibitions strictly added; all merchants coming and going, convoy guards concealing goods—all should be governed by military law.
translations.idiomatic: Old regulations should be reasserted and strictly enforced; merchants and armed convoys concealing arms should be punished under military law.

sentences.zh: 又界上嚴立關候，杜廢間蹊。

translations.literal: Further, on the borders strictly establish passes and scouts, block abandoned bypaths.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, establish strict border checkpoints and close secret paths.

sentences.zh: 城保之境，諸所課仗，並加雕鐫，別造程式。

translations.literal: Within fortified settlements, all assigned weapons should receive carved inscriptions, separately made patterns.
translations.idiomatic: In every fortified district, assigned weapons should be engraved with standard markings.

sentences.zh: 若有遺鏃亡刃，及私為竊盜者，皆可立驗，於事為長。

translations.literal: If there are lost arrowheads or missing blades, and private theft, all can be immediately verified—advantageous for affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Lost arrows or stolen blades can be quickly traced—highly effective.

sentences.zh: 又鉅野湖澤廣大，南通洙、泗，北連青、齊，有舊縣城，正在澤內。

translations.literal: Further, the Juye marsh and lakes are vast, south connecting Zhu and Si, north linking Qing and Qi—there is an old county seat right within the marsh.
translations.idiomatic: The vast Juye marshes connect south to the Zhu and Si rivers and north to Qing and Qi; an old county seat lies within them.

sentences.zh: 宜立式脩復舊堵，利其埭遏，給輕艦百艘。

translations.literal: It is fitting to establish regulations and restore old dikes, profit their dam controls, provide a hundred light warships.
translations.idiomatic: We should restore the old dikes, improve sluice controls, and supply a hundred light warships.

sentences.zh: 寇若入境，引艦出戰，左右隨宜應接，據其師津，毀其航漕。

translations.literal: If raiders enter the territory, lead warships out to battle, left and right adapting to circumstances in response, seize their army's fords, destroy their river transport.
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy invades, sortie with warships, respond flexibly on both flanks, seize their crossings, and destroy their supply routes.

sentences.zh: 此以利制車，運我所長，亦微徹敵之要也。

translations.literal: This is using advantage to control chariots, deploying what we excel at—also subtly penetrating the enemy's essentials.
translations.idiomatic: This turns our advantages against them and strikes at the enemy's weak point.

sentences.zh: 承天素好弈棋，頗用廢事。

translations.literal: Chengtian by nature loved playing go and quite used it to waste affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian was fond of go and often neglected his duties for it.

sentences.zh: 太祖賜以局子，承天奉表陳謝，上答：「局子之賜，何必非張武之金邪！」

translations.literal: The Founder bestowed on him board pieces. Chengtian presented a memorial in thanks. The Emperor replied: 'The gift of board pieces—must it not be Zhang Wu's gold!'
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor gave him a chess set; He Chengtian thanked him in a memorial, and the Emperor replied: 'Must a gift of chess pieces be Zhang Wu's gold?'

sentences.zh: 承天又能彈箏，上又賜銀裝箏一面。

translations.literal: Chengtian could also play the zither; the Emperor again bestowed one zither with silver fittings.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian also played the zither, and the Emperor gave him a silver-mounted zither.

sentences.zh: 承天與尚書左丞謝元素不相善，二人競伺二臺之違，累相糾奏。

translations.literal: Chengtian and Left Assistant Minister of the Masters of Writing Xie Yuansu were not on good terms; the two vied to watch for violations of the Two Departments, repeatedly impeaching each other.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian was on bad terms with Left Assistant Minister Xie Yuansu; the two spied on each other's infractions at court and repeatedly denounced one another.

sentences.zh: 太尉江夏王義恭歲給資費錢三千萬，布五萬匹，米七萬斛。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal the Prince of Jiangxia Yigong annually was given supplies: cash thirty million, cloth fifty thousand bolts, rice seventy thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Marshal Prince Jiangxia Yigong received annual stipends of thirty million cash, fifty thousand bolts of cloth, and seventy thousand piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 義恭素奢侈，用常不充，二十一年，逆就尚書換明年資費。

translations.literal: Yigong was by nature extravagant; expenses often did not suffice. In the twenty-first year he presumptuously went to the Masters of Writing to exchange next year's supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong was extravagant and his stipend never enough; in year twenty-one he improperly obtained next year's allowance from the Ministry of Revenue ahead of time.

sentences.zh: 而舊制出錢二十萬，布五百匹以上，並應奏聞，元輒命議以錢二百萬給太尉。

translations.literal: By old regulation disbursements of two hundred thousand cash or five hundred bolts of cloth and above all should be memorialized to the throne. Yuan directly ordered deliberation to give the Grand Marshal two million cash.
translations.idiomatic: By regulation any disbursement over two hundred thousand cash or five hundred bolts had to be reported; Yuan directly authorized two million for the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 事發覺，元乃使令史取僕射孟顗命。

translations.literal: When the matter was discovered, Yuan then had a clerk take the Vice Director Meng Yan's written order.
translations.idiomatic: When this was discovered, Yuan had a clerk forge Vice Director Meng Yan's authorization.

sentences.zh: 元時新除太尉諮議參軍，未拜，為承天所糾。

translations.literal: At the time Yuan had newly been appointed Grand Marshal Consultant and Staff Officer but not yet taken office—he was impeached by Chengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan had just been appointed staff officer to the Grand Marshal but had not taken office; He Chengtian denounced him.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，遣元長歸田里，禁錮終身。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly angered, sent Yuan to return long to his native fields, imprisoned for life.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious and sent Yuan home to his estate under lifetime house arrest.

sentences.zh: 元時又舉承天賣茭四百七十束與官屬，求貴價。

translations.literal: Yuan then also impeached Chengtian for selling four hundred seventy bundles of fodder to officials and seeking a high price.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan also denounced He Chengtian for selling four hundred seventy bundles of fodder to officials at inflated prices.

sentences.zh: 承天坐白衣領職。

translations.literal: Chengtian was punished to serve in office in plain white.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian was reduced to serving in office as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 元字有宗，陳郡陽夏人，臨川內史靈運從祖弟也。

translations.literal: Yuan, courtesy name Youzong, was a native of Yangxia in Chen commandery—cousin once removed of Lingyun, Administrator of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, styled Youzong, was from Yangxia in Chen commandery and a cousin of Xie Lingyun, Administrator of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 以才學見知，卒於禁錮。

translations.literal: Known for his talent and learning, he died under imprisonment.
translations.idiomatic: Esteemed for talent and learning, he died under house arrest.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，承天遷廷尉，未拜，上欲以為吏部，已受密旨，承天宣漏之，坐免官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year Chengtian was transferred to Minister of Justice but had not taken office. The Emperor wished to make him Director of the Masters of Appointment; having already received secret instructions, Chengtian leaked them—punished by removal from office.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-four He Chengtian was promoted to Minister of Justice but before taking office was tipped for the post of Director of Personnel; he leaked the secret appointment and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 卒於家，年七十八。

translations.literal: He died at home, age seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home at the age of seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 先是，《禮論》有八百卷，承天刪減併合，以類相從，凡為三百卷，並《前傳》、《雜語》、《纂文》、論並傳於世。

translations.literal: Previously the Rites Treatises had eight hundred scrolls. Chengtian cut, reduced, and merged them, arranging by category, altogether three hundred scrolls—together with Prior Biography, Miscellaneous Sayings, Compiled Writings, and discourses all transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Rites Discussions ran to eight hundred scrolls; He Chengtian condensed them into three hundred arranged by topic, along with his Prior Tradition, Miscellaneous Sayings, Compiled Writings, and other treatises, all passed down to posterity.

sentences.zh: 又改定《元嘉曆》，語在《律曆志》。

translations.literal: He also revised and fixed the Yuanjia Calendar—the account is in the Treatise on Measures and Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: He also revised the Yuanjia calendar, as recorded in the Treatise on Harmonics and the Calendar.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：治邊之術，前世言之詳矣。

translations.literal: The history officer says: The methods of governing the borders—the former age spoke of them in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Methods of governing the frontier were discussed thoroughly in earlier ages.

sentences.zh: 夫戎夷狡黠，飄迅難虞，必宜完其障塞，謹其烽柝，使來徑可防，去塗易梗，然後乃能禁暴止奸，養威攘寇。

translations.literal: The Rong and Yi are crafty and cunning, swift and hard to anticipate. One must complete their barriers and passes, be strict with beacon fires and watch drums, so that coming paths can be defended and departing routes easily blocked—only then can one forbid violence, stop wickedness, nurture prestige, and repel raiders.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians are cunning and swift, unpredictable; barriers and beacons must be complete so their approach can be blocked and retreat cut off—only then can violence be curbed and raids repelled.

sentences.zh: 漢世案秦舊跡，嚴塞以限外夷，吳、魏交戰，亦以江、淮為疆場，莫不先憑地險，卻保民和，且守且耕，伺隙乘釁。

translations.literal: The Han dynasty followed Qin's old traces, strict passes to limit outer barbarians. Wu and Wei at war also took the Yangzi and Huai as battleground—none did not first rely on terrain's danger, repelling while securing popular peace, both guarding and farming, watching for gaps and seizing chances.
translations.idiomatic: Han followed Qin's frontier system to hem in outsiders; Wu and Wei likewise made the Yangzi and Huai their battleground—all relied first on terrain, protecting the people while farming and fighting, watching for openings.

sentences.zh: 高祖受命，王略未遠，雖綿河作守，而兵孤援闊，盛衰既兆，用啟戎心。

translations.literal: Gaozu received the Mandate, royal strategy not yet far-reaching—though stretching the Yellow River as defense, yet troops were few and aid distant. Rise and decline already had their signs, which opened the barbarians' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu founded the dynasty his power had not reached far; though he extended the Yellow River line of defense, garrisons were thin and support distant—the tide of fortune shifting stirred barbarian ambitions.

sentences.zh: 蓋由王業始基，經創多闕，先內後外，以至於此乎。

translations.literal: Probably because the royal enterprise was just beginning its foundation, many creations still lacking—first inner then outer, leading to this?
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps because the dynasty was newly founded with many institutions still unbuilt—prioritizing the interior before the frontier—that it came to this.

sentences.zh: 自茲以降，分青置境，無圍守之宜，闕耕戰之略，恃寇不來，遂無其備。

translations.literal: From this downward, dividing Qing and establishing borders—no suitability of encircled defense, lack of farming-warfare strategy, relying on raiders not coming, thus having no preparation.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Qing was partitioned and border policy abandoned encircled defense and farming-army strategy, assuming the enemy would not come—until there was no defense at all.

sentences.zh: 周、漢二策，在宋頓亡，遂致胡馬橫行，曾無藩落之固，使士民跼蒼天，蹐厚地，繫虜俘囚，而無所控告，哀哉！

translations.literal: The Zhou and Han two strategies—in Song suddenly perished, thus causing barbarian horses to run wild, never having frontier fortress solidity, making knights and people cramped under heaven, treading mincingly on thick earth, bound as captives and prisoners with nowhere to plead—Alas!
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou and Han strategies died utterly under the Song, so barbarian horsemen ranged unchecked without frontier bastions, leaving officers and people bound captive under heaven with nowhere to appeal—alas!

sentences.zh: 承天《安邊論》，博而篤矣，載之云爾。

translations.literal: Chengtian's 'On Securing the Borders' is broad and earnest; it is recorded thus.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian's treatise On Securing the Borders is comprehensive and earnest—thus it is recorded.
